	On November 9, the four-member female vocal and dance group PassCode held their arena concert PassCode YOKOHAMA BUNTAI 2025 “DESTINEX” at Yokohama BUNTAI in Kanagawa. Marking their first arena performance in about three years and nine months since their 2022 Budokan show, the event was a special occasion for both the group and their fans. On this day, they surprised the audience with the first-ever live performance of their latest song “Liberator,” announced as the opening theme for the TV anime Roll Over and Die, set to begin airing in January 2026. They also revealed that the song will be released as a single on March 4, 2026.

		Published by Micro Magazine, Roll Over and Die is a dark fantasy story about the protagonist, Flum, who, despite having zero stats, is chosen by the God Origin to join the Hero’s Party and continues to push forward alongside newfound companions. PassCode’s opening theme “Liberator” can be heard in the anime’s newly released PV.

	Alongside the single announcement, PassCode unveiled a new artist photo featuring the denim-based outfits worn at Yokohama BUNTAI. The fresh visual marks a shift from their previous images, showcasing a brighter, more pop-inspired style.

It was also announced that the Yokohama BUNTAI concert will be exclusively streamed on U-NEXT, with the streaming start date to be revealed later via PassCode’s official social media. Leading up to that release, several past performances will be available for unlimited streaming: PassCode ASIA TOUR 2024 Final at Zepp Osaka Bayside on November 13, PassCode presents VERSUS PASSCODE 2024 Vol.2 at Spotify O-EAST on November 27, and PassCode Zephyren 10th Anniversary A.V.E.S.T project Kodo at Yoyogi National Stadium First Gymnasium on December 18. About PassCode
PassCode consists of four members: Nao Minami, Kaede Takashima, Hinako Ogami, and Emily Arima. They have a versatile repertoire based on a band sound, punctuated by their distinctive shouts and screams, and have performed at numerous major festivals such as SUMMER SONIC and ROCK IN JAPAN FESTIVAL, earning broad support from both rock enthusiasts and idol fans.

After making their major debut in 2016, they released their first international album Ex Libris PassCode in America, Europe, and Canada under the UK’s JPU Records in October 2018. The track “Ichikabachika” from their 2019 album CLARITY was selected as the opening theme for the TV drama Kakegurui season 2 and the movie Kakegurui. In 2020, their single “STARRY SKY,” which was chosen as the theme song for the drama 182 Days Left, earned them their first-ever No. 1 on the Oricon Weekly Single Chart and Billboard JAPAN Weekly Single Chart. They also made their debut appearance on Nippon Broadcasting System’s All Night Nippon 0.

In February 2022, they held their first concert at Nippon Budokan. In 2023, they embarked on their first US tour, “PassCode US / JAPAN TOUR 2023 -GROUNDSWELL-,” which included stops in Dallas, Los Angeles, and New York, as well as 11 cities and 12 venues in Japan. In June 2024, they moved to Bandai Namco Music Live. Their September release “WILLSHINE” was chosen as the OP theme for season 2 of the anime SHY, and their new song “SKILLAWAKE” was selected as the OP theme for season 2 of As a Reincarnated Aristocrat, I’ll Use My Appraisal Skill to Rise in the World. title: [Honey's Anime Interview] ASH Talks Ultraman, Inspiration, and What’s Next for ASH DA HERO
text:
Once again, we’re thrilled to welcome ASH, the charismatic frontman of ASH DA HERO, for another interview with Honey’s Anime! Known for his powerful vocals and boundless energy, ASH has been captivating audiences both in Japan and overseas with his band’s electrifying performances. Following the release of “Kyoukai Revolution,” the ending theme for the second half of Ultraman Omega, ASH sat down with us once again to talk about his love for the Ultraman series, the creative process behind the new songs, and what fans can look forward to during the band’s ongoing world tour.



		
 
	
    	
			ASH




 

    
         Honey-Chan





Interview with ASH from ASH DA HERO
[gray-hex-decoration]

    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
We love the Ultraman Omega opening and ending themes. How would you describe the connection of “BRIGHT EYES,” and which elements of the series influenced the music and lyrics of the song?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
It’s truly an honor. From NARASAKI, who composed the music, and Matsui, who wrote the lyrics, I received a song of great importance. The moment I first heard the demo, I thought, “This is Ultraman.”

I’ve been a huge fan of the Ultraman series since childhood, right up to now. For all six years of elementary school, I used to write letters to Ultraman. I would even get replies, and reading those letters was part of my childhood.

That’s why, with all my love for Ultraman, I put my heart into singing every single note, hoping to give courage to the children who will grow up watching Omega. Who knows, maybe among those kids, there will be someone who dreams of becoming a musician and one day sings a theme song like I did. I want to keep passing the baton into the future.




    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
You incorporated rap and lyrics into "Missing Link," the ending theme with MindaRyn. Do you prefer rapping or singing, and which do you find more challenging to perform live?

    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Both are part of my expression and my roots. I don’t find either one more challenging than the other. I always strive to give my best and make sure I’m fully prepared.
    


https://youtu.be/vkyJG809-mQ


    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Now, ASH DA HERO is currently on a world tour. What has this experience been like so far? Do you have a road story you'd like to share with your fans?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
It’s been full of interesting experiences. One tour story that stands out is from San Antonio, Texas. When I sang Deep in the Heart of Texas, the audience sang along and clapped with me, which was both wonderful and hilarious! Everyone in San Antonio was laughing, kind of like, “Why?” I really love surprises like that.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
And what can ASH DA HERO fans anticipate for the rest of the dates of the tour? Could you offer a sneak peek into the stage setup or setlist?

    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
We plan to play new songs from our new album. And of course, we’ll play the Omega song as well. A special guest has also been confirmed to join us.
	



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
That's so exciting! So, what are your plans for 2026?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
I’m going to immediately start working on new music. Please look forward to it!



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
We always talk about your amazing career, and how fans have been follow you for so long, but what are some of your preferred songs and music videos that you would suggest to new listeners?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
I’d love for them to listen to HYPERBEAT! It turned out to be an amazing album!
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
      
As always, ASH’s passion for music and his genuine connection with fans shine through in every word and performance. With HYPERBEAT marking an exciting new chapter for ASH DA HERO and more music already in the works, there’s plenty for fans to look forward to. We’d like to thank ASH once again for taking the time to speak with us, and we can’t wait to see what comes next from this unstoppable force of rock.

	Singer-songwriter mekakushe has released a new song, “Snow Globe Galaxy.” This track is a pre-release from the digital album 138 Oku-nen Me no Koi, scheduled for release on November 7, 2025. Written and composed by mekakushe and arranged by Sondai Nishijima, the song is a two-step track that condenses three minutes of technical beats, as if the universe itself were trapped inside a snow globe. The jacket art and music video were created by collage artist kyabeshi.

The jacket art for 138 Oku-nen Me no Koi has also been revealed. It was created by Southeast Asia–based illustrator Meyoco, an Instagram influencer with over 1.17 million followers who also runs her own apparel line. In addition to the main artwork, she drew complementary illustrations, which will appear on acrylic panels distributed as special gifts for the 1st and 2nd stages of mekakushe Planetarium Acoustic Live ~138 Oku-nen Me no Koi~ on November 27.

Mekakushe’s Comment
Snow globes are beautiful and lonely, holding beginnings and endings, a fleeting eternity trapped inside. When I was little, I loved gazing at them. An infinite world fit in the palm of my hand, self-contained, compressed into a single space, and it made my heart race. Music feels the same. It ends eventually, but for a moment, it becomes my own small, enclosed world of beauty. This song is like a snow globe you can listen to, three minutes capturing beginnings and endings, beauty and loneliness, all in one.

	Sondai Nishijima’s Comment
“Snow Globe Galaxy” is the wild card of the album, packed with surprises in its short runtime. Its signature lies in rollercoaster-like twists and technical beats. I asked Mekakushe to tackle many challenging harmonies and choruses (sorry!), and she sang beautifully, bringing to life a one-of-a-kind snow globe. Enjoy!

	Kyabeshi’s Comment
Just like you see different scenes when you flip a snow globe, we’ve packed a variety of scenes into this music video. I’d love to hear how this video, this world, looks to you.

P.S. I secretly hid seven shrimp, Mekakushe’s favorite, somewhere in the video. See if you can find them!

	Meyoco’s Comment
It’s an honor to create an artwork for mekakushe-san’s music. I had a lot of fun creating the illustration from beginning to end. I was given the chance to create the artwork according to my style, which I deeply appreciate. The main theme I wanted to cover is a combination of “time” and “space,” with the motif of the clock being a dominant element in the artwork alongside the girl. I wanted the artworks to look warm and peaceful, the way you would feel when remembering someone you love. I hope my illustrations could serve well as a companion to mekakushe-san’s music.

[en]What You Need to Know: [/en][es]Lo que necesitas saber: [/es] 


	Tokyo (November 3, 2025)- The "HYPNOSISMIC -Division Rap Battle-" movie (hereafter referred to as "HypMovie") began its revival screening at 66 theaters across Japan starting September 2nd, HypMic's anniversary, to commemorate the 8th anniversary of the project's launch. With the revival, HypMovie has finally surpassed the major milestone of 2 billion yen in box office revenue. 

	HypMovie is Japan's "first" interactive movie and made its screen debut on February 21st, 2025 at 85 theaters in Japan. Due to the limited amount of interactive screening equipment, the movie continued its run at a limited number of 60 to 80 theaters in Japan. While there have been many movies in the past that started with small-scale releases of around 10 theaters, gained popularity and expanded to over 150 theaters to become major hits, HypMovie has become the first movie in Japan to surpass a box office revenue of 2 billion yen with fewer than 100 theaters from its opening day. (Source: Kogyo Tsushinsha)

	One of the reasons the movie has been such a hit is due to its interactive nature, the first of its kind in Japan, and which plays a central role in the viewing experience. The outcome of each rap battle unfolding on the screen is decided by the audience via a specialized voting system carried out via smartphone. Viewers vote during the movie a total of 5 times to determine the winner of each battle, which means there are a total of 48 different ways the movie can play out and 7 different endings.
　
	Furthermore, to commemorate the movie's success, the specially-produced video "Claim Victory (Immersive Edition)"—which is being shown at the "HYPNOSISMIC -Division Rap Battle-" exhibition currently in Nagoya—has been uploaded to the official Hypnosis Mic YouTube channel for a limited time.

title: Anime NYC 2025 - Post-Show Field Report
text:
[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	




  
Anime NYC 2025 has come and gone so quickly! Every year, we have to wait till Anime NYC arrives again and begin to prepare. We grab our notepads, think about how to tackle all that’s within the convention halls, and ready our wallets to be emptied by the merchandise we’ll buy and the food we’ll devour! It’s hard not to feel like, when this convention finally starts, it’s over in the blink of an eye...

That being said, we attended 4 days of Anime NYC 2025 and had quite a few experiences, some good and others bad, and that’s why we once more present to you all our post-show field report to entertain you! Read all about our various trials and tribulations, as well as some of the shining moments of this year’s Anime NYC! Now, let’s relive Anime NYC 2025! 
	




	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

		
	
  
    
While the prices have risen pretty dramatically, Anime NYC 2025 was larger than previous years and had a lot more events and big name guests. The prices might be a bit hard to stomach for some but again, it was kind of unavoidable. 
		
  
	

Company/Event Message for Fans/Attendees
  
    
			“Anime NYC is a creation of LeftField Media, an event company made of dedicated fans and convention organizers. Anime NYC is built with tremendous support from Crunchyroll and publishers across the Japanese pop culture industry.”
		
  
	



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

		

What Anime NYC 2025 Did Better Than Before
  
    
In comparison to 2024, Anime NYC 2025 had a lot more to explore. There were plenty of booths, from VTUBERS such as Hololive, where fans of various VTUBERs could join together, sing with them, listen to their randomness, and just enjoy a dedicated gaming hall where various tournaments were being held, like Tekken 8, Street Fighter 6, and even Super Smash Bros! Famous YouTubers like IronMouse and CDAWG VA were there too (sadly, we couldn’t watch them due to time constraints), and that was pretty neat!

There were also a slew of popular voice actors out there for meetups, interviews, and fan questions. Needless to say, this Anime NYC was without a doubt the most varied one to date. Regardless of what type of otaku you are, Anime NYC 2025 had you covered!

There were plenty of booths this year, ensuring a bit more variety than past outings. There was the Hololive stage, where fans of various VTUBERs could join their favorites, sing with them—they performed numerous anime and popular English songs—listen to them talk about silly topics, and even join in as if they were part of the group! Almost every day, Hololive was the loudest event by far, showing just how passionate those fans are.

Those who wanted a more typical anime con affair could scour the floors for merchandise from numerous vendors, like Yen Press, Good Smile Company, Viz Media, and plenty of others. But with how pricey Anime NYC 2025 was, this certainly would stretch your savings a bit. We’d be lying if we didn’t admit we got a ton of figures ourselves, but it was well worth it to show our support to our favorite vendors.

Gaming otaku weren’t left in the dark at Anime NYC 2025! There was a big emphasis on games this year, with an entire floor dedicated to hosting gaming events. Con-goers could play against others in their favorite fighting games like Tekken 8, Street Fighter 6, and even Super Smash Bros! There were also card game tables for all the favorites, like Magic the Gathering, Yu-Gi-Oh, and so on. We even heard that some popular YouTubers like IronMouse and CDawgVA were playing games with the crowd! Due to time constraints, we couldn’t see them ourselves, but from the fan roars, we know they were enjoying the event!

Lastly, there were quite a few panels and voice actor meetups available! Famous voice talent like Kaiji Tang, Christopher Sabat, Aleks Le, AMALEE, and others were there to talk to con-goers, sign merch, or take photos! There were also plenty of panels where con-goers could learn more about numerous industry themes and/or upcoming projects. It would be impossible to see and experience everything in one day, let alone four, but at the very least, you couldn’t say there was nothing to do at Anime NYC 2025! 
    
  
	



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

		

What Anime NYC 2025 Could Have Done Slightly Better
  
    
Unfortunately, Anime NYC 2025 wasn’t without its drawbacks. The first—and most glaring—was overcrowding. We here at Honey’s Anime have been to our fair share of conventions, large and small, and Anime NYC 2025 is a medium-sized one compared to the titan that is Anime Expo. Nevertheless, it was clear that there was either no limit on how many could attend or a false expectation of how many would show up. Lines affected almost everything at the con, from food stalls and vendors to meeting some of the guests. The lines for food stalls were so long at times that they spilled into the non-food vendor areas, which was just terrible. Equally, seeing some of the guests was a nightmare, as lines could go on so long that it would be either impossible to meet them—unless you were there early enough—or by the time you worked your way up to the guest, they were on break or done with their time slot. Seriously, Anime NYC 2026 needs to consider capping ticket amounts or opening more of the Javits Center so there’s more room.

Another issue was the lack of big gaming vendors. Despite scouring the floor, we really only saw a few minor ones. Don’t get us wrong—we were more than thrilled to see Honor of Kings with their Detective Conan collaboration and Kaiju No.8, which we could play briefly—it looks and plays incredibly well for a mobile/Steam game. Yet, we were expecting some bigger gaming panels, maybe from Capcom or even SEGA. We get that this is an anime convention, but it does have a lot of gamers who attend, and we would have liked some more gaming content.
    
  




	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

		

Cosplay Was Amazing, Once Again
  
    
As you can see, there was a lot of cosplay, but we always try to look for the more unique ones. In our gallery, there are the usual cosplayers, but we are very happy to include some funny and stylish ones from Anime NYC 2025! All cosplayers who had individual photos taken were asked for permission beforehand, so thank you all for posing for Honey’s Anime! Hopefully next year we’ll see even more from newer anime airing!
		
  




	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

	



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

	



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

	

Anime NYC 2025 was great despite some issues here and there. In our opinion, more people attending shows a greater appreciation for the convention, which is wonderful—but it also means that more of the Javits Center should be opened to help remedy the crowd. All things considered, we had a great time and would love to thank Anime NYC 2025 for allowing us the privilege to attend as press once again! We hope to see you all at Anime NYC 2026, which will no doubt happen after the success of this year! For now, though, we’re going to rest our tired wings and take a much-deserved nap…

	SANDA, by Paru Itagaki (creator of BEASTARS), is an unconventional Santa Claus action series set in near-future Japan, where extreme measures are taken to protect children amid a sharp population decline. The anime premieres in Japan on October 3, 2025, with exclusive worldwide streaming on Prime Video beginning October 4 at 2:53 a.m.

	Today, the main visual and full promotional video were released. The main visual depicts Daikoku Welfare Academy, where protagonist Sanda and his classmates study, with school principal Hifumi Oshibu—who exerts extreme control over the children—looming in the background. Santa Claus dramatically bursts through glass, symbolizing hope in a bleak future.

	The reveal also introduces key characters and cast: Toshihiko Seki voices 92-year-old principal Oshibu, who obsessively clings to youth through repeated full-body plastic surgery, and Hiroaki Hirata plays Saburo Yagiuda, ace of the St. Nick Pursuit Unit dedicated to capturing Santa. Comments from both voice actors are included below.

	The promotional video, showcasing Science SARU’s dynamic animation, portrays a world where children are tightly controlled and Santa is freed from a curse through wishes. It also features the first voice lines from the newly revealed characters Oshibu and Yagiuda.

The opening and ending themes have also been announced. The opening theme, “Childlike Adults,” is by yama, and the ending theme, “Diary,” is by Soushi Sakiyama. Comments from both artists are included below.


https://youtu.be/PG9F1afLT-Y
	
	New Characters and Voice Cast Revealed, with Comments!
		Hifumi Oshibu (Voiced by Toshihiko Seki)
The 92-year-old principal of Daikoku Welfare Academy, where Sanda and his classmates study. Obsessed with youth, he repeatedly undergoes full-body plastic surgery. He has an extreme dislike of adults and goes to abnormal lengths to protect and monitor his students’ every move.

		Comment
1. How did you feel when you were cast as Oshibu in SANDA? And what message do you have for fans looking forward to the series?
Of all Paru Itagaki’s works, SANDA was one I was especially interested in. And among her many characters, Hifumi Oshibu’s personality stands out. I approached the role with a fresh mindset to fully capture his unique presence. Please look forward to it!

2. Since this is an action series featuring Santa Claus, is there anything you’d want to ask him for?
If Santa Claus were like the one in this series, every Christmas would be far more exciting! But if a real Santa Claus existed, I think I’d ask him to promise a future where children everywhere can live in safety.

		Profile
Born: Tochigi Prefecture
Major roles: Muzan Kibutsuji in Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba, Medama Oyaji in Birth of Kitaro: The Mystery of GeGeGe, and Hansuke Doi in Nintama Rantaro


		Saburo Yagiuda (Voiced by Hiroaki Hirata)
The ace of the St. Nick Pursuit Unit dedicated to capturing Santa. Twenty years ago, he inflicted a serious injury on Santa Claus.

		Comment
1. How did you feel when you were cast as Yagiuda in SANDA? And what message do you have for fans looking forward to the series?
Although my character only appears partway through the story, I was warmly welcomed and had a great time recording. These days, there aren’t many productions where we go out drinking after recording, but with this one, everyone’s a heavy drinker, and I got dragged out until late at night every time. I’m counting on you, Murase!

2. Since this is an action series featuring Santa Claus, is there anything you’d want to ask him for?
Although I’m over 60, I’m still full of worldly desires. I think I’d ask Santa to help me become the kind of person who can say, “I have nothing more to wish for.”

		Profile
Born: August 7, 1963, Tokyo
Major roles: Sanji in ONE PIECE, Sha Gojyo in Saiyuki, and Beryl Gardenant in From Old Country Bumpkin to Master Swordsman
		
		Opening Theme Song
“Childlike Adults” by yama (Sony Music Labels Inc.)

		Comment from yama　　　
What does it mean to be an adult? Simply growing older does not necessarily make you one. Likewise, I do not believe that being young automatically makes someone a child.
Silently carrying pain is both weakness and fragility, and facing it alone might be a clumsy way of avoiding reality.
I once thought there was virtue in growing older while holding onto that fragility. But in recent years, whether with people close to me or through music, I have gradually begun to open my heart.
The line between myself and others has not changed, yet through connecting with others I discover new sides of myself. I do not think of myself as either an adult or a child, but rather believe that people possess both qualities at any age.
It is not about clinging to one side or deciding what is right or wrong. I have simply realized that I want to trust someone, and that is also a way of trusting myself.
To anyone else who feels caught between the two, I hope this reaches you.

		Ending Theme Song
“Diary” by Soushi Sakiyama (Sony Music Labels Inc.)

		Comment from Soushi Sakiyama
I’m honored to perform the ending theme. I felt a deep connection to Kazushige’s inner struggle, caught between adulthood and childhood, and I poured those emotions into the song. In a world without clear answers, where each person’s idea of justice collides, the way Kazushige moves forward with so many voices in his heart has moved me time and again. I hope you enjoy the song together with the anime.

title: BEYBLADE X US National Tournament Brings Anime-Worthy Duels to Los Angeles Anime Expo 2025
text:
[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	




  
TAKARATOMY held its first-ever Beyblade X National U.S. Open-Class Qualifier as part of their BEYBLADE X World Championship 2025, hosted inside the Los Angeles Anime Expo ― marking 25 years since the brand first arrived in the U.S.!  If that’s not hinting at how exhilarating this contest was, keep on reading!
 




	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

		
	
  
    
A surge of excitement radiated through the Entertainment Hall,  and for those attendees who visited, it was common to hear the thrilling chant of “3… 2… 1… Let it RIP!!” echoing through the venue. It was an instant attention-grabber for fans young and old who had ever watched the anime or played Beyblade themselves. Impossible to miss, the Beyblade championship arena drew in thousands of spectators over the four days of the convention. On Saturday, July 5, the tournament reached its final stage, attracting 128 competitors who made history by participating in the first official U.S. Open-Class single-elimination showdown.    
  
	



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

		
	
  
    
Not only did contestants experience the structure of an official tournament, like those held in Japan, but this was also foreshadowing, as the champion of the U.S. tournament would advance to the Beyblade X World Championship 2025 in Japan, with an all-expenses-paid trip to represent the United States.

Honey’s Anime had the opportunity to sit front row for the final showdown, and trust us when we say the crowd was filled with extreme positivity, immaculate energy, and a raging hype that built up even more each round.
    
  
	



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

		
	
  
    
Starting with the third-place match, TMS faced Cosmo Dragon, a duel that TMS slayed with a 3-point victory, a survivor finish!
    
  




	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

		
	
  
    
Next up was Yushwa, cosplaying as Takao Kinomiya, the protagonist of “Bakuten Shoot Beyblade,”the first series of the Beyblade anime. His opponent was ElenaBEY, a woman who won the hearts of the crowd thanks to her meme-worthy championship picture. Despite their playful demeanor, the two finalists delivered a seriously intense battle that was just as exciting as duels we’ve seen in the anime!    
  




	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

	

  
    
This battle was truly worthy of being the last match in the national US championship, it had it all. Mid-air collision, survivor finish, and a double knockout finish you name it! This battle was intense. In the end, ElenaBEY’s trusty Dran Buster 5-60 LF pulled through, helping her make a comeback after a draw and score two points with a knockout to win the championship.
    
  




	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

	



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

	

  
    
The Entertainment Hall erupted with intense cheering for ElenaBEY, who secured her ticket to Tokyo this October for the global finals. But she wasn’t the only one being celebrated. The crowd was going wild for all eight top competitors who delivered thrilling action throughout the day.

We had the opportunity to do a quick interview with the top 3, and this is what they had to say:
    
  


Interview with TMS, 3rd Place



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	



Q: Did you come today with the intention of winning, or just having fun? Did you expect to make it this far?
A: I came all the way from Texas to win. I was waiting since 2018 for this moment and the experience was insane; I’m just really happy to get to compete. 
Q: How did you hear about this tournament at AX, and was this your first time in a tournament? 
A: I’m a content creator who focuses on competitive Beyblade so of course I knew about this and I’ve been in 32 tournaments just in the past 6 months to make it here. 
Q: After today’s defeat, do you plan on changing your strategy?
A: I plan to constantly change my style as always, trying out different styles of my interest.

Interview with Yushwa, 2nd Place



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	



Q: After such an intense spin-off against ElenaBEY, how do you feel?
A: Exhausted! And stressed, but I wanted to make sure people had a good time watching the match.
Q: We’ve noticed you have quite a fan following among the crowd. Do you have a few words to share with your fans?
A: SoCal is still strong.  We need more tournaments, more opportunities to give a chance to more players. Don’t stop playing until Beyblade becomes an e-sport! Until then, we need to take care of each other. I hope everyone had fun watching my matches and that I could deliver what the crowd wanted to see.

Interview with ElenaBEY, US Champion



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	



Q: In a competitive scene like Beyblade X, how do you feel as a woman having won this championship in a game predominantly played by men?
A: Now I feel proud to represent women in Beyblade, not only as the U.S. champion. I want to show that Beyblade is for everyone, and I hope my win influences more women to join the world of Bey.
Q: Did you come to this tournament focused on winning?
A: I never expected to reach the top, or win! My friends helped me out with the knowledge of what Beyblade to pick, they helped me a lot through the preliminaries so I feel this win is for everyone who helped me. I am surprised I won!
Q: Were you surprised that the champion would have a chance to trip to Japan to join the BEYBLADE X World Championship 2025?
Is this your first time going?
A: No, it wasn’t a surprise. People were talking about the chance to compete in the World Championship in Japan. It’s not my first time in Japan, but I’m really looking forward to the shopping and food in Tokyo!
Q: Any final words for your fans?
A: The most important thing is to have fun and keep playing!



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	



  
    
The Beyblade X National Tournament not only made history in the U.S but also delivered an unforgettable experience to fans and players alike. Tokyo, get ready—passion is on its way from the U.S.

Known for its unique blend of American streetwear aesthetics and traditional Japanese visuals, Enter the Garden marks a bold departure from Japan’s traditional anime production model. Taniguchi shared his thoughts on creative freedom, artistic philosophy, and how Azuki’s community is reshaping what it means to create anime.



		
 
	
    	
			Goro Taniguchi


	

 

    
         Honey-Chan





Interview with Goro Taniguchi
[gray-hex-decoration]

    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
You've worked within the traditional Japanese pipeline of transforming an idea into anime. How has your experience differed working with Azuki, especially given their focus on short-format anime and changing how anime is produced?
			
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
In the past, I usually worked with stories that already existed. This time working with Azuki, there was no original material to reference. So the process started with me asking, “Is this the right path?” and then presenting my ideas to Azuki. Sometimes those ideas were rejected, but the key has been constant communication between us. I’ve had to understand Azuki’s goals and translate that into animation. This open, cross-partner dialogue is very different from working with Japanese publishers or studios that produce anime, manga, or light novels in a traditional format. So far, it’s been a refreshing and exciting change for me.		
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Enter the Garden seems to be inspired heavily by modern American street fashion and traditional Japanese elements. Could you tell me more about what inspired the look and aesthetic of the world?
			
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
As I mentioned earlier, we first asked the Azuki side to show us what kind of things they were thinking about and wanted to do, as well as what kinds of fan art existed. From there, we picked out the parts of their ideas that we understood or that we also thought were cool. Staff members who understood the concept arranged everything in the form of Episode 1, Episode 2, and Episode 3.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Are there plans to introduce other cultural aspects from different countries in future episodes?
			
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
That’s something I intentionally avoid. Digging deeper into the reasoning, the staff working on the project had already had that kind of idea in the past; however, we have agreed on focusing on one style identity with room for subtle influences. If I direct that they should include other cultural references, it may hinder the staff’s creativity. That’s something I would like to avoid. I believe that giving the team creative freedom yields better results. I purposely place staff who can generate something good without being influenced. To give more details, for episode 1, I assigned staff who had worked on things other than anime. In episode 2, I assigned staff who could also illustrate the 1980s to 2000s era’s anime style. By doing this, I can ensure each episode has its own uniqueness.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
What can you tell me about the character’s personality? Are they in any way influenced by Azuki’s company philosophy or your vision as a director?			
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
As for episode 1, the world setting is Azuki’s idea but the characters were created under our direction. In episode 2, we featured Azuki’s original characters, but I directed how they came to life on screen. Episode 3, which hasn’t been released yet, both the characters and the world were created as a way to further expand our interpretation of Azuki. 
	



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
When you talk about expanding in artwork and animation technique, in what way do you mean exactly? Are you talking about introducing techniques like rotoscopying or stop motion animation?
			
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
It’s not about technique for the sake of technique. It’s about philosophy and how to express an idea visually. If stop motion helps convey that concept, we’ll use it. But technique is secondary to intention. What matters most is expressing the underlying message in a compelling way.	
	



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Between episodes 1 and 2 of Enter the Garden, there seems to have been some evolution regarding animation. How did Azuki grow during this process, and what did you learn?			
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Absolutely, there’s been growth. Originally, I had my plans for episodes 2 and 3. But after finishing episode 1, Azuki suggested new ideas for episode 2, probably ideas that reflected community feedback. I didn’t see these suggestions as just coming from a company, but as a petition from the fans. So I made adjustments to my original vision. Anime is a business, yes, but it’s also for the fans. Their input helped shape the direction of the project.
	



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
What message or experience do you hope to deliver to the anime community with Enter the Garden?
			
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Whatever message I want to convey can only be delivered through the anime itself. That’s why I create. What makes this project special is that it listens to the fans and translates their voice into animation. That’s what truly matters.
	



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        	
Are you hoping to bring more creators into the Azuki community, or is this anime laying the groundwork for something bigger?
			
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Whether it's from the wide anime community or Azuki’s community, if you are a creator, the more eyes on your work, the better. My goal isn’t just to cater to the Azuki community, it’s to reach the wider anime audience. By doing this, if that draws more people into Azuki, that’s something I can feel happy about. If that happens, you can say creating Enter the Garden anime was successful.
	



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Working with legends like Tatsuyuki Tanaka on Enter the Garden must be a unique experience. How do you foster an equal creative environment for industry veterans?
			
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
The answer is very simple. As the director, I define clear creative boundaries. I explained the project and everyone’s responsibilities at the start. Mr. Tanaka understood exactly what his role was and where his creative domain lay. Once that’s clear, I don’t interfere unless someone steps outside their zone. That mutual respect is what keeps the environment clear of issues.
	



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
      
Goro Taniguchi’s approach to Enter the Garden reveals a balance between personal creative vision and open collaboration with both Azuki and its growing community. This experimental project isn’t just about breaking anime conventions in format and production, it’s about exploring how far you can go when fan voices, corporate goals, and experienced direction meet halfway. With more episodes on the horizon and an evolving aesthetic, Enter the Garden may just be a blueprint for a new era of anime production where creators like Taniguchi continue to innovate beyond borders.

title: [Honey's Anime Interview] Takayuki Miyauchi and Kenta Wakisawa From T-SPARK at the Los Angeles Anime Expo 2025
text:
At Anime Expo 2025 in Los Angeles, Honey’s Anime had the opportunity to sit down with two key figures driving strategy and innovation in the world of collectible figures and character goods: Takayuki Miyauchi (Senior Assistant Manager of the Marketing Team in the Collector Business Group, Hobby Character Business Division) and Kenta Wakisawa (Assistant Manager of the R&D Team in the same division).

In our conversation, Miyauchi-san and Wakisawa-san offered a rare glimpse into the heart of the industry—and how they plan to keep surprising collectors worldwide.



		
 
	
    	
			Miyauchi



	
 
	
    	
			Wakisawa


	

 

    
         Honey-Chan





Interview with the T-SPARK Team
[gray-hex-decoration]

    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
T-SPARK is described as a brand for adult hobbyists. What’s the vision behind creating a unified brand for adult hobbyists and has that vision evolved since its launch?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
			Wakisawa: Our division handles long-running IPs like Transformers and ZOIDS, and we’d already been developing products for a high-target demographic. So under the company-wide policy of increasing lifetime value and expanding customer segments, we decided to take the lead in expanding offerings for kidults (adults with a playful spirit).
			
Although the toy and hobby businesses may seem similar, their structures differ significantly. So for this initiative, we assembled a project team that included members beyond just management and our division. Together, we held in-depth discussions, looking ten years ahead, on how our company should approach and expand the kidult market from a medium- to long-term perspective.

Through those discussions, we realized that Takara TOMY now targets a wide spectrum of customers, from children to adults, and that this requires different approaches for each segment in both product development and marketing. In the hobby category especially, we recognized the need to clearly define and separate our kidult offerings. For instance, our official YouTube channel previously featured videos for both kids and adults, but to deliver more relevant content to each audience, shouldn’t we consider separating the channels?

There are also differences in focus between children’s and adults’ products when it comes to quality and ethical standards, raising the need for distinct criteria. As we looked to expand the kidult segment over the medium to long term, it became clear that clearer boundaries were needed. That led to the decision to launch a separate label for kidult-focused collector items. This was the rationale behind T-SPARK, and our vision has remained unchanged since its launch.		
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
How do you prepare your marketing strategies to reach its intended audience, particularly in international markets like here in the USA?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
			Wakisawa: We only began expanding into the U.S. market in 2025, so we’re still in the early stages, testing various strategies to see what works. While overall trends in the U.S. market aren’t drastically different from those in Japan, action figures are a particularly strong category, and in recent years, Japanese IPs have become extremely popular. By leveraging that interest in Japanese culture and applying Takara TOMY’s hobby expertise, we aim to develop new products and build awareness of the T-SPARK brand. Our appearance at AX this time is part of that effort.

Looking ahead, we plan to roll out a variety of collaboration products featuring popular manga, anime, and other globally loved content. We’re also working to strengthen our online presence, centered around our North American e-commerce platform, Tommy Plus. At the same time, we want to create more offline touchpoints, such as places where fans can see product samples in person.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
How do you approach targeting adult collectors over younger fans, especially when working with huge titles like My Hero Academia that attract multi-generational audiences?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
			Miyauchi: We believe that expanding the T-SPARK brand is essential to gaining traction with adult collectors. The new figure brands we’ve launched will offer a wide range of products, from affordable to high-end, designed to appeal to various fan demographics.

SPARK Fig is a mid- to high-priced series targeting adult collectors, while the COLLEKAZARO series is designed not only for adult collectors but also to appeal to female fans.

By offering a diverse range of products targeting a broad fan base, we hope to raise awareness of the T-SPARK brand among as many people as possible.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
      
Although brief, our conversation with Miyauchi-san and Wakisawa-san shed light on how Takara TOMY is shaping the future of its collector business through T-SPARK, a brand built with a playful spirit, yet crafted with the sophistication and quality adult fans expect. From the long-term vision that led to creating a distinct label, to early steps in expanding into the U.S. market, and the thoughtful strategies behind engaging multi-generational fandoms with lines like SPARK Fig and COLLEKAZARO, it’s clear that T-SPARK represents more than just figures—it’s a commitment to redefining what it means to collect, connect, and celebrate Japanese pop culture on a global scale.

title: fhána and Sachiko Kobayashi Celebrate the Release of New Theme Songs for Miss Kobayashi’s Dragon Maid Movie: “Parade of Tears” and “Bokutachi no Hibi”
text:
[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="Author/Photographer: Junichi Tsukagoshi" url="" ]
	



[en]What You Need to Know: [/en][es]Lo que necesitas saber: [/es] 


	A special event was held on July 13, in AEON LakeTown mori, to celebrate the release of the new opening and ending songs for the Miss Kobayashi’s Dragon Maid movie!


	Kyoto Animation’s newest work is a heart-warming tale about family and the bonds that unite us. Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid: A Lonely Dragon Wants to Be Loved is the latest installment in the animated series, which started airing in 2017. Of course, seeing these popular scenes from the original work on the big screen has been a huge hit with the audiences!

	On July 13th (Sunday), fhána and Sachiko Kobayashi made an appearance at AEON LakeTown mori, to help kick off the release of their respective opening and ending songs, “Parade of Tears” and “Bokutachi no Hibi.” Since Koshigaya in Saitama Prefecture serves as the story’s backdrop, the location couldn’t have been more fitting.

Tickets for the priority viewing area (which came with the purchase of one of the CDs being released that day) sold out in a flash. The space was packed with spectators before the event even started. Since there might not be enough time during the concert itself, Kevin Mitsunaga (sampler, etc.) gave the crowd a primer on the choreography for “Parade of Tears” during their rehearsal, and asked them to lead the rest of the audience for the real deal.

	
	About the Event	
The event itself started right at 1:00 p.m., with fhána’s performance of one of the definitive opening themes from the anime, “Rhapsody of Blue Sky.” Towana (vocalist) got the audience all fired up as her voice rang out from the stage, accompanied by Junichi Sato on the keyboard, and Kevin on the metallophone. The crowd sang and clapped along, clearly enjoying their amazing pop performance.

Pausing just long enough to announce their group name, fhána launched straight into “Love Supreme!”, the opening song from Miss Kobayashi’s Dragon Maid S. Towana and Kevin’s bright, bouncy rap makes it a memorable song, and their fast-paced repartee, mingled with the crowd’s applause, created an euphoric atmosphere.



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	



During the MC segment, they mentioned that they were pleased to be visiting Koshigaya for the first time. And most people in attendance raised their hands when asked whether or not they’d seen the Miss Kobayashi’s Dragon Maid movie. On seeing that, Junichi mentioned that their next song had been “inspired by Kanna’s (CV. Maria Naganawa) tears.” Then, Kevin gave the crowd a quick review of the choreography before launching straight into the movie’s opening theme, “Parade of Tears.” The crowd was quick to put those moves into action when the chorus came around. Though, for an upbeat pop song, there’s an element of melancholy to it.

Since fhána has created each of the series’ opening songs, their lyrics and melodies have really stuck with the listeners. Junichi joined in the dancing partway through, livening up the performance even further—but was probably going to limit that to this event. (Or possibly the upcoming Animelo Summer Live event.) ”Yeah, I think that’s it for the dancing,” he said, mellowing the mood out.
	


	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

	

This was the perfect transition into the ending theme’s portion of the event. The audience called out for “Kobayashi-saaan!” (just like the titular character), Sachiko Kobayashi took to the stage to sing “Bokutachi no Hibi.” The message there is that “Nothing is certain, but that’s easy to forget. We might have met here by accident, but that’s a kind of miracle. These precious moments ought to be cherished.” 

Standing on stage in her stunning red dress, Sachiko’s gentle voice rang out, instantly catching everyone’s attention. Her voice couldn’t be better suited to a song that talks about how the “usual” things are the foundation of life. The performance was only a few minutes long, but it was a wonderfully moving piece that truly encapsulated the movie.

After that touching finale to a rousing mini concert, fhána closed out the event by signing CDs that the fans had purchased.

Miss Kobayashi’s Dragon Maid: A Lonely Dragon Wants to be Loved is a huge hit! fhána and Sachiko Kobayashi’s opening and ending songs have gone on sale to great acclaim! Plus, it was okay to take pictures and videos at this event, so there are probably plenty of those to check out on social media.

title: “HYPNOSISMIC -Division Rap Battle- Movie”& “Uta no☆Prince-sama TABOO NIGHT XXXX”Anime Expo 2025 Screening Report
text:
[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	



[en]What You Need to Know: [/en][es]Lo que necesitas saber: [/es] 


	Fans of anime, manga, games and cosplay from all over the world had the opportunity to attend a special double screening from King Records of "HYPNOSIS MIC -Division Rap Battle- Movie" and "Uta no☆ Prince-sama♪ TABOO NIGHT XXXX" at Anime Expo, the largest anime event in North America.
	
	Here’s our report of the screening held at The Novo on Saturday afternoon!

	HYPNOSISMIC -Division Rap Battle-
I arrive at my second-floor front-row seat 15 minutes before showtime. While it doesn't seem too crowded, I look to the first floor front-row seats to see several groups of what appear to be fans in cosplay, checking their penlights. Looking at the screen, I see a QR code to download the app that will be used to determine each battle's winner, as well as how to vote during the screening. This won't be your typical theater experience — it's something entirely new, where the outcome of the movie lies in the hands of the audience.



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	


	
"Hypnosis Mic -Division Rap Battle-", or "HypMic" for short, is a story set in a world where armed conflict is illegal, and territory is instead gained via rap battles using Hypnosis Mics, special microphones that interfere with human psyche. Teams representing each division compete in the "Division Rap Battles", led by the all-female team Party of Words.

Battles are fought in teams of 3, with 6 teams total:
→ Buster Bros!!!: Ikebukuro Division
→ MAD TRIGGER CREW: Yokohama Division 
→ Fling Posse: Shibuya Division
→ Matenro: Shinjuku Division
→ Bad Ass Temple: Nagoya Division
→ DOTSUITARE-HOMPO: Osaka Division
	


	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

	

The team that wins the first and second stages will proceed to the final stage where they can challenge the Party of Words in battle. The full movie covers events up until the final stage, but for this specially-edited AX closing screening, only up until the second stage is shown.

But what sets this movie experience apart is the mid-movie voting, done via a mobile app called CtrlMovie. After each battle's conclusion, a 10-second countdown begins on the app where viewers vote for the best-performing team by tapping the division's logo. After a few seconds, the winning team is displayed and the story continues.

As the fate of each team is decided by the audience, even for those who might not call themselves fans, the tension in the room as the countdown begins is electric. As the result flashes on the screen, the audience erupts—united in a chorus of both joy and heartbreak that reverberates through the theater.

The characters' reactions and comments differ depending on the results, which makes every viewing a unique thrill. In total there are a whole 48 different ways the story can play out. Fans will watch them all, no doubt.

I realize it's almost time for the movie to start and take a last look around behind me to see that the seats are now filled to overflowing, with even more people standing behind the last row. The first floor is of course also packed. Seeing this spectacle, I feel the excitement building as the MC stirs up the crowd. Then, the screening finally starts.

Over the roars of the crowd, the first thing we see are clips introducing each division. Every team is met with screams of excitement, with the waving penlights changing color each time. I now realize that the pre-screening penlight checking was for this all-important color-changing operation. The introductions perfectly capture each team member's characteristics and their relationships with each other. Next is the opening video, where we get to hear everyone’s singing voices, and includes every character. The battleground is set. The cheers were so loud for every single division that I could not even guess which one might win.
	


	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

	
	
And now for the rap battles to begin!

	First stage, first battle
Buster Bros!!! Vs Bad Ass Temple
The battle between Ichiro (Buster Bros!!! leader) and Kuko (Bad Ass Temple leader), who are former teammates, is a must-see. 

Time for the vote of destiny. After a short silence, Buster Bros!!!’s logo appears on the screen, followed by loud cheering and crying.

Up on the screen, Kuko approaches Ichiro and they congratulate one another. Fans cheer out warmly.

	First stage, second battle
MAD TRIGGER CREW Vs DOTSUITARE-HOMPO
Samatoki (leader of MAD TRIGGER CREW) and Sasara (DOTSUITARE-HOMPO leader) were also once partners on the same team. They know each other inside out — every strength and every weakness. But today isn't a duel. It's a team battle, where the team that unites their strengths to the fullest seizes victory.

Voting time again. A few seconds pass in silence before DOTSUITARE-HOMPO's logo flashes onto the screen. The crowd erupts.

In the face of his loss, Samatoki speaks gracefully and the crowd’s comforting words left an impression.

	First stage, third battle
Fling Posse vs Matenro
Ramuda (leader of Fling Posse) and Jakurai (Matenro's leader) say they hate one-another, but what is the truth...?

During the battle their faces were so close they almost touched, which resulted in cheering and screaming throughout the venue every time.

Once again it is time to vote, and after a short silence, Matenro's logo appears and is met with loud cheering and screaming.

The resentment between the two leaders fades and Jakurai approaches Ramuda amicably, but Ramuda's irritation at Jakurai's unintentionally condescending remarks makes for an amusing conclusion.

The second stage is a tournament between the three teams that won the first stage.

Buster Bros!!! Vs DOTSUITARE-HOMPO vs Matenro

Fate once again is in our hands, and this time the choice is between three teams. Cheers for each team echo across the venue, but it's DOTSUITARE-HOMPO who claim victory. The cheering and the screaming reach their climax.

At long last, it's time for the final battle with Party of Words. The MC reappears and the screening comes to an end. While the winning division was not my first choice, the result made me very interested to see what a battle between the Kansai team DOTSUITARE-HOMPO and the all-female team Party of Words would look like.

hypnosismic-movie.com/voting-status/ax2025
You can also check out the results for all the screenings held in Japan here:
hypnosismic-movie.com/voting-status/results
	
	"Uta no☆Prince-sama TABOO NIGHT XXXX"
After a (small) switch up in the audience between HypMic and Uta☆Pri fans, the MC introduces the next feature and turns the fans' excitement all the way up! This movie is the third theatrical release for Uta☆Pri and contains a full-length live concert as well as a brand-new animation featuring QUARTET NIGHT.

The "Uta no☆Prince-sama♪ Maji Love" series is a part of the larger Uta☆Pri multimedia franchise, originally a romance visual novel aimed at women. The movie features four members who form the idol unit QUARTET NIGHT:
→ Reiji Kotobuki

* JINN-Ω-RAY (all members)



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

	
	
The audience cheered and changed the color of their penlights for each idol, and joined in every single idol call. And in perfect Japanese, of course.It was just like being at an idol concert in Japan.

After seeing both movies, I was reminded that the love and enthusiasm of fans here rivals — or perhaps even surpasses — that of fans in Japan. From the happy faces of the fans after the screening, there is no doubt that this passion and love will continue to grow.

title: Official Report: Bandai Namco Music Live Festival at Anime Friends 2025! Southeast Asia Concerts Also Confirmed!
text:
[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	



[en]What You Need to Know: [/en][es]Lo que necesitas saber: [/es] 


	The Bandai Namco Music Live Festival returned to Anime Friends 2025, held in São Paulo, Brazil from July 3 to 6. This marks the second consecutive year the festival has appeared at South America’s largest anime convention, which draws an annual attendance of around 150,000.
	
	Bandai Namco Music Live manages labels including Lantis, SUNRISE Music, Kiramune, MoooD Records, and UNIERA, and is home to a diverse roster of artists. On the festival’s opening day, four acts took the stage: ASH DA HERO, STEREO DIVE FOUNDATION, Nowlu, and MindaRyn.

	TUfave is excited to announce its new collaboration jewelry collection with the TV anime “Attack on Titan”. These necklaces (5 designs total) delicately capture the attractiveness of the characters and the series' world, inspired by iconic scenes. Each piece features a simple design centered around a large natural stone, creating "collaboration jewelry for adults" that subtly blends into daily life.

	Nowlu Kicks Off the Show with Her Anisong Debut
Nowlu opened the festival with a confident performance that defied the fact it was her first-ever live show. She began with “Arika” (GUILTY GEAR STRIVE: DUAL RULERS) and “yoin” (Wingman).

“I’m so happy to have my first live show here in São Paulo,” she said with a smile, drawing warm cheers. She followed with “Stuck on you” (More Than a Married Couple, But Not Lovers), creating a calm, intimate moment that brought the crowd together. Her debut ended to enthusiastic applause.

Next up was a DJ set by ASH DA HERO member DJ Dhalsim. The crowd couldn’t help but dance as he spun one anisong hit after another: “Ai♡Scream!”, “Bokura wa Ima no Naka de” (Love Live!), “Shika-iro Days” (My Deer Friend Nokotan), and “Hare Hare Yukai” (The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya). The energy of anisong swept through São Paulo, connecting fans across generations.	
	
	“Brazil, I’m back!” MindaRyn Returns with a Smile
MindaRyn took the stage next, returning for a second year in a row. “Brazil, I’m back!” she called out with a big smile before launching into a set of three powerful yet gentle songs: “Daylight” (Arifureta: From Commonplace to World’s Strongest Season 2), “Shiny Girl” (SHY), and “Fireworks” (Why Raeliana Ended Up at the Duke’s Mansion).



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

	
	
During her MC segment, she asked, “Was anyone here last year? Thanks to those seeing me for the first time, too!” connecting warmly with the audience. As part of her world tour Hello New Friends, which began in June 2025, she performs special covers of songs from her label, Lantis. For Brazil, she sang “Rhapsody of Blue Sky” (Miss Kobayashi’s Dragon Maid, originally by fhána) and “Sparkling Daydream” (Love, Chunibyo & Other Delusions, originally by ZAQ).

She followed with a high-energy rock trio: “HIBANA” (Sengoku Youko: The Reformer Siblings Arc), “SURVIVE” (Why Raeliana Ended Up at the Duke’s Mansion), and her breakout hit “Like Flames” (That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime Season 2), which has surpassed 22 million views on YouTube. Her explosive performance had the entire venue fired up.

	STEREO DIVE FOUNDATION: Sound and Vision in Perfect Sync
STEREO DIVE FOUNDATION (R・O・N) made his Brazilian debut with a 17-song medley set to anime visuals. Highlights included “ALPHA” (Moriarty the Patriot), “Renegade” (GANGSTA), and the fan-favorite “STORYSEEKER” (That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime Season 2), which has surpassed 10 million views on YouTube.



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

		
	
The set closed with “Daisy” (Beyond the Boundary), with the crowd gently swaying their hands in unison. R・O・N recalled fans in Chile asking, “Aren’t you coming to Brazil?” and now that he had, he understood why. The crowd responded with knowing nods and applause.
	
	Surprise Collaboration with Ultraman Omega!
After a brief pause, the word “Ultraman” appeared on the screen, instantly stirring the crowd. MindaRyn returned to perform “BLACK STAR” (Ultraman Blazer), followed by an appearance from Ultraman Blazer himself, drawing cheers and excitement.
	


	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

	

The event then transitioned into the new series Ultraman Omega. ASH performed the opening theme “BRIGHT EYES,” while MindaRyn and ASH debuted the ending theme “Missing Link” live for the first time. The blend of hero action and rap interplay brought the crowd’s energy to a fever pitch.

	ASH DA HERO Brings the Festival to a Climactic Close	
ASH DA HERO took the stage for the grand finale, joined by Dhalsim (DJ), Sato (bass), and WANI (drums). Kicking off with “Super Sonic,” they followed with “YELLOW FEVER DANCE” and “Hankou Seimei” as the crowd pumped their fists and sang along.

They kept the energy high with “LA VIDA LOCA,” already a live anthem despite being a recent release, then surprised the audience with “Octave” and “Beast Mode,” insert songs from Blue Lock: Episode Nagi, accompanied by anime footage. After introducing the members, they launched into “Judgement,” the opening theme for the anime’s second cour. The crowd erupted, singing along as ASH stepped off the stage shouting, “Sing it, Brazil!”



	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

		

They closed with a final roar of “We are ASH DA HERO!” as ASH triumphantly returned to center stage.

	A Powerful Finale: All Artists Unite

For the final act, all performers returned to the stage at ASH’s invitation for the first-ever band performance of “Trinity” (That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime: The Saga of How the Demon Lord and Dragon Founded a Nation). ASH took on Takuma Terashima’s part in this rare collaboration, thrilling fans. The concert closed with a group photo and a wave of thunderous applause.
	


	
		
			
		
		[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	

		

The excitement didn’t stop even after the main festival ended. On Friday the 4th, all the performers held a meet-and-greet and Q&A panel. On Saturday the 5th, ASH DA HERO took the stage, followed by STEREO DIVE FOUNDATION and MindaRyn on Sunday the 6th.

In its second year, the Bandai Namco Music Live Festival at Anime Friends powered up with even stronger artist × IP collaborations. Alongside powerful performances, the festival featured fan events and previews of new projects, highlighting the full potential of anisong.

The anisong wave that swept Brazil in 2024 has firmly taken root—and is still growing!

	Next Stop: Southeast Asia!

The Bandai Namco Music Live Festival isn’t just heating up Brazil; it’s heading to Southeast Asia next. The festival will appear at COS-MIC 2025 in Malaysia on September 13, and AniEx 2025 in Bangkok, Thailand on November 22.

The anisong excitement born in São Paulo is spreading across borders, forging new connections through music. The journey of the Bandai Namco Music Live Festival is only just beginning.
