title: [Honey's Anime Interview] BEYBLADE X Interview with Masahiko Yamazaki, Hisato Takaoka, and Makoto Muraki at the Los Angeles Anime Expo 2025
text:
As part of the BEYBLADE X World Championship, the company behind BEYBLADE held the U.S. National qualifier at Anime Expo 2025 in the Los Angeles Convention Center. Honey’s Anime had the opportunity to interview Masahiko Yamazaki (Head of Global Beyblade Business), Hisato Takaoka (General Manager of Beyblade), and Makoto Muraki (Specialist on the Beyblade Design Team). Let’s see what they had to say about BEYBLADE X’s first tournament appearance at AX!



		
 
	
    	
			Takaoka



	
 
	
    	
			Yamazaki




 
	
    	
			Muraki


	

 

    
         Honey-Chan





Interview with the BEYBLADE Team
[gray-hex-decoration]

    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Why did you choose Anime Expo as the venue for the U.S. National qualifier? What goes into organizing an event of this scale here?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
BEYBLADE launched in Japan in 1999, and in the U.S. in 2000. That means it has been 25 years since BEYBLADE first arrived in America. Last year was our first time bringing BEYBLADE to Anime Expo and we were very, very surprised and excited to find so many adult fans here. We have always believed the potential of American fans and community, and seeing their passion firsthand was a very great opportunity for us. That’s why we wanted to return and hold the tournament at this year's event.

BEYBLADE started just as a toy, but we’ve been aiming towards making it an entertainment sport, that’s why we thought about Los Angeles, the city of entertainment. Anime Expo is a very, very huge event so, in line with our branch’s story, this is a very suitable opportunity and a suitable event at AX. If you had the chance to come here during the morning (Saturday, July 5, 2025) there were so many people in line, we were not expecting so many fans to show up! Last year, BEYBLADE was here, but this year is the first time that we’ve held a tournament. We could not have imagined the number of people who attended. We were pleasantly surprised and very impressed with the number of attendees.
    







    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
What are you hoping that fans take away from this event, or what were you expecting to show fans by holding this tournament here at AX?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
From what I’ve seen, there’s a great opportunity to further grow and support adult tournaments in the U.S. I want to give hope that in the future, we will have more and more events for the American fans. While at the booth, I wondered why 200, or 300 people had gathered here, staying all the time around the stage area; it got me thinking that maybe this is a very, very rare opportunity to witness an official BEYBLADE tournament.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
I wanted fans to take away the experience of an official tournament. I hope that those people who participated in the Anime Expo Tournament, go back to their hometowns and do the same as they did here. We formally introduced how to participate in a BEYBLADE tournament, showed them not only the format, but the experience, and how it goes after you lose or win a match, where you shake hands, etc. That’s the experience I hope they take from this event. 
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
After seeing the popularity of the BEYBLADE X tournament in Anime Expo, are you planning on coming back to AX next year or maybe plan on holding other official tournaments in other conventions across the U.S.?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Yes, as BEYBLADE X we plan to come to Anime Expo next year. We hope to expand with other tournaments or activities, as well as participate in other major U.S. conventions, working together with Hasbro, our U.S. partner.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
With BEYBLADE X growing in popularity, what’s your vision for the expansion of the franchise in the next decade?  Do you see it expanding into things like virtual or augmented reality battles, or is the focus more on growing physical product availability, especially here in the U.S.?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Seeing that there are many new technologies like AI, AR, or VR as you mentioned, in the case of BEYBLADE it had a weird introduction into the metaverse world through Roblox. Right now, nearly 40 million visitors from around the world have joined the BEYBLADE world on Roblox. I can see that technology is important, but from what I can see the most important thing is the community. BEYBLADE fans are encouraged to enjoy the brand in many ways, so it has great potential to cultivate a community no matter what technology it expands to. But we’ve committed to grow the community rather than focusing on introducing the brand to new technology.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Why did you choose Roblox as the “community builder” for BEYBLADE?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
In Japan, Roblox is not really popular yet, but in the U.S.A, as well as other parts of Asia it's really popular. BEYBLADEs’ strength is that they can provide a physical experience, at the same time, this is our weakness. We want fans to enjoy BEYBLADE globally, but as of right now, Roblox is the answer the fans have created. And the fantastic thing is that you can play it from anywhere.

[Takaoka proceeds to take out his phone, which is already online on Roblox and actively spectating a BEYBLADE match between real people that are online at that moment]		
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
The players of that BEYBLADE world in Roblox, the total of Japanese players is maybe around 5% but the other 95% are from all over the world; number one is currently Thailand, followed by Mexico and the U.S.A. That's why we embraced Roblox, since it’s a global platform that surpasses the barriers and restrictions of our physical limitations.		
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
When designing parts for BEYBLADE X with competitive players in mind, how do you strike a balance between performance, durability, and customization? Is one prioritized more than the others, or is it always a compromise?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Those three elements you mentioned are very, very important. First of all, BEYBLADE X is a product that can be enjoyed by children and adults, so our priority is safety. At the same time, it has to be truly thrilling and fun to play. Although it seems at odds with safety the features that make the game exciting—like high-speed, intense collisions are essential for our products so it is a big challenge for us to pursue both aspects. We try not to have tradeoffs or compromises, they try to deliver all those points at the highest possible “level”, This is something we really take care of when thinking about new model designs.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
As a competitive game, BEYBLADE must often introduce different "battle strategies". I see BEYBLADE X has a gimmick called "X-dash" Could you walk me through how you come up with these strategies?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
BEYBLADE X physical contact is really important. “Physical contact” is the base keyword in the company, so everyone keeps it in mind when creating the product. If it goes faster, would it be interesting? If it falls apart, will it be interesting? Those kinds of unique ideas are always brought forward by the team and we bring it to life as a demo product by the design team to test it out. After everyone has experienced it and it makes sense as a strategy, then the idea will move on to the next level until it makes it to the actual product. One thing we’re always taking care of is that we don’t create only an idea, but also create a demo product to test it out within the team.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
As for battle gimmicks like the X-Dash, so far what has been the most challenging or interesting gimmick that you have created?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
3rd generation BEYBLADE Burst. This was the first time that the toy would be torn apart, breaking into pieces. That gimmick introduced in the 3rd generation was challenging because the point was for them to break apart on purpose, but also you should be able to put it back together. On top of that, we had to achieve for it to spin super fast and all the pieces would fly out all over the place, so safety was a challenge. Before this model, the arena did not have the guard piece, so we had to come up with the arena barrier too. 
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Now that you have seen the popularity of BEYBLADE X in Anime Expo, and of course, Anime Expo caters to an Otaku culture, do you have in mind any collaboration with some big anime title? For example, a series of toys inspired by big IPs?
			
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
In Japan, we’ve had experience collaborating with celebrities and sports groups. We won’t deny any future collaborations with any anime IP. We have already  collaborated with major IPs like Star Wars and Marvel featuring characters like Skywalker or Spiderman, we even have a collaboration with FC Barcelona, a legendary European multi-sports club based in Catalonia.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
I want to ask you all for your personal experience watching the popularity of the BEYBLADE X booth and seeing all the fans there as well as the competitive U.S. Bey community playing in the tournament. Has anything surprised you? Has the U.S. player base inspired you in any way? How’s the US community different from the Japanese community? Any personal feelings that you’d like to share about your experience at Anime Expo and the BEYBLADE Championship? 
			
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
As I expected, United States fans are really full of emotion. Most of the American　fans are shouting “Woo, I did it! I did it!”. I like this style of celebrating, it's something I am really glad to see, hahaha.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
During BEYBLADE’s panel event at AX, we played the first episode of our new anime season. The fans there were very very excited and had a good reaction. But we not only talked about the animation, we also talked about BEYBLADE as a product and the community was very curious about how we design our toys, about the making process. It gave me the impression that the U.S. fans are extremely curious about BEYBLADE, so I enjoyed their reaction to our panel.  
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
When I saw the participants of the tournaments and noticed the kind of Beys that they use I thought their selections were interesting. Usually, when you compete in tournaments, the ultimate goal should be to win, right? But seeing the U.S. participants, they are using the BEYBLADEs that they really like, ones that they have emotional attachments to. The ratio is a lot higher in the U.S. than in Japan. The way that fans enjoy BEYBLADE X here in the U.S. is wider, so that’s the point of view I gained from this experience and I will take it into consideration for future product design.  
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
      
The passion and enthusiasm surrounding BEYBLADE X at Anime Expo 2025 was undeniable. It's clear that BEYBLADE continues to evolve as more than just a toy, it’s a global phenomenon fueled by community, creativity, and competition. With plans to return and expand further into U.S. events, the future of BEYBLADE is spinning faster than ever!

title: Jaleco Sports: Goal! - A Nostalgic Kick from the 8-bit and 16-bit Era
text:
[ad_top1 class="mb40"]



  
    
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eOhDLZ9gdEg
    
  



  
Most of you probably weren’t even born back then, but some of us still remember what football games were like before they turned into lootbox fests catering only to online competitors. Back in the day, there were tons of different titles and approaches to the sport, and most of them had their own unique charm, offering countless hours of fun with friends and siblings.

Among the standouts, the Goal! franchise was probably our favorite… and now it’s back in full glory, with both classic games bundled into one awesome package!
	




  
Football Unites the World
			
	
  
    
Yes, that’s actually one of FIFA’s recent slogans (the organization, not the video game series), and it perfectly captures one of the highlights of this new bundle.

Originally developed by Tose and published by Jaleco (both Japanese companies) Goal! (known in Japan as Moero!! Pro Soccer) debuted in 1988. It was later localized for North America and Europe, with slightly different versions released in each region. Thanks to its popularity, a sequel followed in 1992, launching globally. But things weren’t as straightforward as they might seem…
			

  
    
      

        
        [sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
    
  
  			
			
Because the games were released in different regions and on different consoles, there are a number of notable differences—not just in the titles, but in the content itself. For instance, the lineup of national teams varies by version. In the Japanese release of Goal!, Uruguay and the USA are not included; instead, players get Northern Ireland and Scotland. Goal! Two features even more regional variation: the Japanese version includes teams like Colombia, Ghana, and Austria, while the Western release swaps them out for Canada, Mexico, and Venezuela. Meanwhile, the USSR and West Germany are present in the NES version but were omitted from the SNES port.

Fortunately, this new bundle includes all versions of both games, giving players access to every regional team, no matter where they were originally released.
    
  




  
A Perfect Title for Collectors!
		


  
    
      

        
        [sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
    
  
  
	
  
    
Another feature we absolutely loved is the inclusion of all the original cover art and instruction manuals. Back in the '80s and '90s, reading and re-reading those little booklets, or proudly displaying them on your shelf, was a big part of the whole video game experience.
			
Sure, these games aren’t exactly complex in terms of controls or mechanics—after all, most systems back then only had a couple of buttons to work with. In fact, most of the instructions now feel like plain common sense to today’s players. Still, having access to the original manuals feels oddly refreshing. And best of all, you can switch languages with a single button press.
    
  




  
And What About the Gameplay?
  


  
    
      

        
        [sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
    
  
  	
	
  
    
The most notable addition to this bundle is the ability to rewind time at any moment (like in some racing games), whether it’s to stop a goal from being scored, avoid a yellow or red card, or simply get a second chance after completely shanking a shot into the stratosphere.
			
Was it necessary? Probably not. Does it feel like cheating? Absolutely, and football purists will no doubt see it as a disgrace to the sport. But hey, it’s 100% optional, so no harm done… right? If anything, it’s just a modern safety net for retro frustration. 
    
  
	

  
    
      

        
        [sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
    
  
  

  
    
No one expects games from four decades ago to stand toe-to-toe with modern sensations like EA FC, PES, or even Rematch. But firing up a few Goal! or Goal! Two matches with friends, whether out of nostalgia or curiosity, depending on your age, can still be a blast.
			
Sure, we don’t see ourselves playing these games non-stop for days, but we genuinely enjoyed re-adapting to the punishing controls and arcade-style gameplay. Plus, there's something charming about scoring goals with national teams from countries that you don’t typically find in other football games, or that don’t even exist anymore. Nevertheless, if you like competing online, you can compete against other players on the monthly leaderboards! 
    
  	







  
Final Thoughts
  
  
  
Jaleco Sports: Goal!, the remake developed by Sickhead Games and Rock It Games, is one of those bundles we’re just happy to have in our library, ready to launch now and then for a few laughs and a trip down memory lane.

The game is available for Windows PC via Steam and GOG. It's been announced there will be a PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch release later this year.

	Bandai Namco Music Live Inc. will begin accepting entries for the third round of its anime song choir project ChoieL on July 1, 2025.

	ChoieL is an ongoing online choir competition that was launched in August 2022, with a second round in March 2024. Round 3 brings back the 22 songs from previous editions and adds new selections from Bandai Namco Music Live’s SUNRISE MUSIC label, for a total of 28 eligible songs. As before, the contest features two categories: Full and Short.

	Returning to the judging panel are Sohei Miyoshi (Choral Conductor / Secretary General of the Tokyo Choral Association / Planning and Supervision) and composer Tatsuya Tanaka, both of whom have served as judges since the first round.

	Joining this round as official ambassadors is ARCANA PROJECT, an artist group from Bandai Namco Music Live’s Lantis label. A promotional video featuring the group is now available. ARCANA PROJECT will also serve as guest judges and present a new “ARCANA PROJECT Award.”

	Entries will be accepted from July 1 to August 31, 2025, with both the Full and Short categories held concurrently. We look forward to your enthusiastic participation!

	Participating Judges

	Sohei Miyoshi (Choral Conductor / Secretary General of the Tokyo Choral Association / Planning and Supervision)
It’s been three years since ChoieL began, and thanks to your support, we’re now entering our third round. The six new songs for Round 3 include titles that will resonate with an even wider range of generations than the original 22. With the addition of new arrangers, we believe this round offers more than ever for both anime song fans and choral music lovers alike. We hope ChoieL continues to be a place where you can express your passion to the fullest.

	Tatsuya Tanaka (Composer)
The ChoieL online choir competition is now entering its third round. The full lineup of 28 songs, including the six new additions, offers an exciting and enjoyable blend of anime songs and choral music in terms of song selection, arrangement, and composition. The past two competitions were full of unforgettable moments, and we’re already looking forward to seeing how participants will express themselves this time. If you have a passion for anime songs and choral music, that’s all you need to get started. We can’t wait to see your entry!

	Official ChoieL Ambassadors & Judges
	
	ARCANA PROJECT (Lantis/Artist)	
A vocal unit consisting of Usa Sakurano, Hana Hanamiya, Shion Aida, Hikaru Amano, Yuka Shidomi, and Sakura Yoshino, co-produced by DEARSTAGE and Lantis. With a tarot card-themed group motif, they bring a diverse range of songs, including anime theme songs, to life through their distinctive vocals and performances.

	Comment:
We’re ARCANA PROJECT, and we’re honored to take part in the ChoieL anime song choir project as both official ambassadors and judges. As a group brought together by our love of anime and singing, we’re truly excited to be involved in such a wonderful initiative. 

Through our work as ARCANA PROJECT, we’ve come to feel that what matters most isn’t technical skill, but the joy of singing while making eye contact, the comfort of shared breath, and the freedom to express music from the heart. Discovering your own voice and connecting with others through song are deeply meaningful and precious experiences. 

We hope this project brings those same experiences to many people. We can’t wait to hear your voices.

As the first step of this project, we hosted our first online choir competition in August 2022, and 50 groups participated to showcase the fresh appeal of anime songs.

	KADOKAWA CORPORATION will co-host the novel contest, "MyAnimeList x Honeyfeed Writing Contest 2025 - THE ISEKAI presented by KADOKAWA," in partnership with qdopp Inc. and MyAnimeList Co., Ltd. The contest will be held on Honeyfeed, a novel submission platform operated by qdopp, with the goal of discovering exceptional storytelling talent from around the world.

	This contest aims to discover fresh talent who can craft stories with the potential to stand alongside industry-defining titles like Overlord, Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, The Rising of the Shield Hero, Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation and Sword Art Online. As an added bonus, the  contest features a special guest in the jury panel: Aneko Yusagi, writer of The Rising of the Shield Hero. Winners even receive personalized feedback from this renowned and experienced Isekai author, an incredible chance to gain insight directly from one of the most successful storytellers in the genre.
	
	Comment From Satoshi Arima, Project Manager and Editor in Chief of MF BOOKS
In recent years, Japanese anime has seen a surge in global popularity. Many of these popular anime titles originate from light novels. At KADOKAWA, we are constantly seeking new talent to create the next big hit. Amid this trend, an increasing number of stories styled after Japanese light novels are being posted on overseas novel submission platforms. These platforms are emerging as hubs for content and creators with the potential to achieve widespread success not only in Japan but around the world.
	
	In response to this global trend, KADOKAWA has launched the Global UGC Publishing Project as part of its Global Business Acceleration Program, which supports new business ventures targeting international markets. This project aims to discover global talent through overseas novel platforms and bring “internationally-born” light novels to audiences both in Japan and worldwide.
	
The MyAnimeList x Honeyfeed Writing Contest 2025 – THE ISEKAI presented by KADOKAWA marks the first step in this initiative. Moving forward, the project will expand through initiatives such as a Traditional Chinese writing contest hosted on KadoKado - the novel serialization platform operated by KADOKAWA TAIWAN CORPORATION - as well as the publication of selected winning titles from the JNC Original Light Novel Contest organized by M12 Media LLC.

	SANDA is a manga by Paru Itagaki, creator of BEASTARS, which won the Grand Prize at the 2018 Manga Taisho along with three other major manga awards. Set in a near-future Japan where extreme measures are taken to protect children amid a drastic population decline, the story depicts an unconventional Santa Claus hero in an action-packed tale. The anime adaptation is produced by Science SARU, the studio behind DAN DA DAN and Scott Pilgrim Takes Off. It is set to premiere in Japan on October 3, 2025, with a world premiere also confirmed for Anime Expo.

	Alongside the broadcast date announcement, the second teaser trailer has been released. It showcases a world shaped by extreme overprotection amid a super-declining birthrate, focusing on the classmates of protagonist Kazushige Sanda (voiced by Ayumu Murase) at Daikoku Welfare Academy. How is Santa Claus treated in a Japan where children have almost disappeared? And how will Sanda’s interactions with classmates like Fuyumura develop? Stay tuned for more updates!
	
	New Characters and Voice Cast Revealed, with Comments!
Alongside the release of Teaser PV #2, several new characters have been revealed! 
Umeka Shoji voices Shiori Fuyumura, who discovers Sanda’s identity and sets out to save her missing best friend. Her friend Ichie Ono is played by Anna Nagase. Yuuki Shin voices Hitoshi Amaya, Sanda’s roommate, and Misato Matsuoka plays Nico Kazao, Sanda’s fiancée.
Comments from the cast have also been released!

	Voice Cast of Sanda’s Classmates Revealed!
	Shiori Fuyumura (Voiced by Umeka Shoji)
A 14-year-old classmate of Sanda who stands over 182 cm tall. She seeks help from Santa Claus to find her friend Ono, who suddenly went missing. To break the curse and revive the sealed Santa, she threatens Sanda with a deadly blade.

	Comment
1. How did you feel when you were cast as Fuyumura in SANDA? And what message do you have for fans looking forward to the series?
Meeting Shiori Fuyumura during the audition was such a powerful experience that it feels like she’s become a constant presence in my life. I poured everything I have into this role. I’d be thrilled if SANDA reaches a wide audience.

2. Since this is an action series featuring Santa Claus, is there anything you’d want to ask him for?
A liver so strong that it can handle any alcohol.
	
	Ichie Ono (Voiced by Anna Nagase)
A classmate of Sanda and best friend of Fuyumura. She suddenly disappeared from their class, and her whereabouts remain unknown. The school considers her dead, but Fuyumura is determined to search for her with Santa Claus’ help.

	Comment
1. How did you feel when you were cast as Ono in SANDA? And what message do you have for fans looking forward to the series?
Ono was a role that really challenged me. I struggled a lot while developing the character, and I constantly felt a sense of anxiety and tightness in my chest. I hope that feeling comes through in Ono’s portrayal. Please look forward to the broadcast!

2. Since this is an action series featuring Santa Claus, is there anything you’d want to ask him for?
When I was a kid, I was always the one receiving presents, so this time, I’d like to give something back. Maybe I could help out? Like riding in the sleigh with Santa and delivering presents around town! That sounds like fun.
	
	Hitoshi Amaya (Voiced by Yuuki Shin)
Sanda’s roommate, also known as “Prince Amaya.” He is one of the few who know Santa Claus’ secret and wants him to return to fulfill an important wish.

	Comment
1. How did you feel when you were cast as Amaya in SANDA? And what message do you have for fans looking forward to the series?
I’m really excited to be voicing Amaya in SANDA. I enjoyed bringing out his mysterious charm through my performance. This story really makes you reflect on what it means to be an adult. It’s a wonderful series, so please be sure to watch it!

2. Since this is an action series featuring Santa Claus, is there anything you’d want to ask him for?
I’d love to ask Santa Claus for a Nintendo Switch 2. Even if I don’t get one, just a chance to win the pre-order lottery would be great. I’ve been good, so please! I’d like to play racing games on it!

	Nico Kazao (Voiced by Misato Matsuoka)
Sanda’s fiancée, chosen by the country from birth. She’s a realist who wants to rebel a little before becoming a “responsible adult.” She always acts freely and often swears.

	Comment
1. How did you feel when you were cast as Nico in SANDA? And what message do you have for fans looking forward to the series?
When I first learned about Nico, I was deeply captivated by her complete freedom from any constraints. She might be someone who truly understands the preciousness of the present moment. I’m genuinely happy to be able to bring her to life! Please watch as these lovable characters struggle and grow together. I poured my heart into this role and had a great time. Thank you for your support!

2. Since this is an action series featuring Santa Claus, is there anything you’d want to ask him for?
I love eggplant, so I’d want lots of dishes like deep-fried eggplant soaked in light dashi and mapo eggplant!

title: [Honey's Anime Interview] Celebrating TRUE's 10th Anniversary!
text:
Miho Karasawa, who also goes by the stage name TRUE, has just released her 10th anniversary album titled "TRUE the BEST" on February 26 (her debut date)! You may know her for her passionate vocal style and straightforward lyrics in theme songs for anime series like Buddy Complex, Gargantia on the Verdurous Planet, Maria the Virgin Witch, Sound! Euphonium, and many others.

Although she has been active as an artist since 2000, she debuted under the name TRUE in 2014, quickly becoming a powerhouse singer, flawlessly performing numerous opening and ending themes each anime season.

We had the lovely opportunity to interview TRUE once more, to talk about the future and reflect on these ten years full of hits and challenges.



		
 
	
    	
			TRUE




 

    
         Honey-Chan





Interview with TRUE
[gray-hex-decoration]

    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
It’s been a year since our last conversation, and we're so happy to be chatting with you again! So, you recently released an anniversary album, packed with 30 songs and numerous hits. Was it challenging to select and arrange the tracks for this album? And if you had to choose, which song would you say is your favorite?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
This release includes singles, lead tracks from albums, and key songs that represent my musical journey over the past ten years. With the exception of the first and last tracks, the songs are arranged in the order they were released. It starts with the first track, “TRUE,” and ends with “DelighT,” with the capital T at the end representing the T in TRUE. I wanted it to begin and end with TRUE, which is how the tracklist took shape. Every song holds a special meaning to me, so it’s hard to pick just one favorite.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
The Limited First Edition includes a Blu-ray featuring two performances: TRUE Live Sound! vol.6 Encount, held at NHK Hall, and Sayonara Nakano Sunplaza Music Festival: TRUE Live Sound! vol.7 Ensemble, held at Nakano Sunplaza, both from 2023. Can you share any memorable anecdotes or special moments from these performances?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
For me, live performances are life itself. I’m truly grateful to have these moments recorded. I hope that even those who couldn’t be there can still feel the passion of the shows through the Blu-ray.
    


https://youtu.be/x6fUsfL8UKw


    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
And how about your most recent live event, TRUE 10th Anniversary Live Sound! Final Shuutaisei at Zepp DiverCity this January? How was that experience?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
That show was the perfect way to wrap up my 10th anniversary. It was my first time performing in a large live house, and the audience’s energy was even greater than I had imagined. I felt that it was a meaningful milestone not just for me, but for the fans as well, marking the end of a decade. Throughout the anniversary year, I held various types of live shows, and I plan to use what I gained from those experiences moving forward.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Now it's time to celebrate your first decade as an artist, but given everything you've accomplished so far, we imagine you're already planning your next steps. Are you currently working on any new songs or projects to be released soon?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Yes, I’m trying various new things and plan to put even more effort into live performances both in Japan and overseas. Since last year, I’ve been doing joint live shows with other artists, and through these interactions, I’m working to expand my musical range.
			
Another goal for the future is to create a theme song for a tokusatsu anime. I will continue my music activities, dreaming of the day that wish comes true.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
In May, you performed three new shows in Japan as part of your TRUE Live Tour PLAY! vol.1 -ReCoda-. How did you prepare for these events?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
This time, I did my very first hall tour. I felt like I received so many gifts and warm congratulations for my 10th anniversary, and so many people came out to celebrate with me at my shows. 
		
I’m going to use all that support as fuel to make each live performance a success from this 11th year onward, which will help me grow even more. It’s not exactly going back to my roots, but I’m planning to perform with the same band lineup as my very first live, carefully arranging each song to deliver it thoughtfully. In June, I’m also holding my first-ever Asia tour. It’s a new challenge to see how much I can convey beyond borders and language barriers. I’ll do my best!			
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
We'll be looking forward to this!

And to close our interview, could you share a message for our readers, many of whom have followed our previous interviews and are passionate about your music?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Thank you always for your support. I’m truly grateful to receive encouragement from people in many countries through social media. Your words keep me motivated. From now on, as an anisong singer, I will continue doing my best to share Japanese anime culture and anisong culture with all of you. I look forward to the day we can meet someday.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
      
We've been listening to this new album since release day, and it brings back so many memories!

At Honey’s Anime, we’re deeply passionate about TRUE’s music and have had the pleasure of witnessing her incredible growth over the years. If you’re new to her work and eager to discover more, be sure to check her out on social media.

	U/M/A/A has announced that it will release a second installment of “TechnoByobu,” an art piece that combines the spirit of techno with the traditional Japanese craft of folding screens, in 2026. This new series, titled “TB-02: The Ghost in the Shell,” is based on Shirow Masamune’s legendary cyberpunk series The Ghost in the Shell.

	“TechnoByobu” is an art piece of a new era that reimagines the works of internationally and domestically acclaimed artists as folding screens made from wafer-thin golden brass leaves, a craft that has been handed down in Japan for over 500 years. The artworks, vividly depicted in vibrant colors on folding screens made entirely of golden brass leaf, have attracted attention as a fusion of traditional and modern art. The first piece, “TB-01: Electronic Fan Girl,” which was inspired by the album artwork of YMO (Yellow Magic Orchestra), generated significant buzz.

“TB-02: The Ghost in the Shell,” based on the world-famous science fiction work The Ghost in the Shell (Shirow Masamune/Kodansha), utilizes the physical medium of a folding screen with cybernetic visuals, creating a next-generation visual that merges past and future.

	
	Scheduled for release in 2026 as part of a series themed around traditional Japanese elegance, the first work in the series boldly features Motoko Kusanagi and the Fuchikoma from Shirow Masamune’s original 1991 manga, on a golden brass leaf background.

	Prior to the release, U/M/A/A will unveil the first prototype of the series at Design Shanghai 2025 (designshanghai.com) to be held in Shanghai, China, from June 4, 2025.

	What is TechnoByobu?	
TechnoByobu’s “techno” originates from the Greek word téchnē, meaning art, technique, or skill. It embodies more than just practical know-how; it’s a philosophical concept that encompasses the intelligence and creativity behind craftsmanship, as well as the futuristic expression of electronic music. Rooted in this background, “techno” is not only the origin of the word “technology” but also a layered term that blends cultural and artistic innovation.
Based on this philosophy, TechnoByobu is composed of three elements:
・Artwork that evokes futurism (art)
・Byobu (folding screens), a traditional Japanese craft kept alive by artisans (skill)
・Digital certificates guaranteed by technology (technique)

By overlapping these elements, TechnoByobu culminates as an art piece that expresses the multifaceted nature of “Techno.” Moving forward, it will continue to explore new possibilities of expression in collaboration with diverse talents both in Japan and abroad.

	About The Ghost in the Shell	
“The Ghost in the Shell” is a science fiction manga series written by manga artist Shirow Masamune, which began serialization in 1989, in Kodansha’s “Young Magazine Pirate Edition.”

The story revolves around Motoko Kusanagi, a full-body cyborg with exceptional skill in both cyber and conventional warfare. With the rank of Major, she leads the aggressive unit “Shell Squad” as they confront highly intricate and sinister crimes. With its realistic art style, the series’ narrative explores the fusion of humans and technology, delving into cyberpunk elements and philosophical themes, while deeply examining topics such as personal identity.

The series has been expanded into various forms including theatrical and TV animations, as well as games. Each of these adaptations offers its own unique story, interpretations, and expressions, distinct from the original manga.

At this year’s 2025 Design Shanghai, starting June 4, TechnoByobu’s second installment, “TB-02: The Ghost in the Shell,” will be unveiled to the world for the very first time. During the exhibition, visitors will have the opportunity to see the prototype up close.

In its founding year of 1905, Rekiseisha developed a groundbreaking scientific technique that had never been seen before: foil-pressed paper using brass leaf that was just as beautiful as the traditional gold foil (hon-kinpaku) but far more resistant to discoloration over time. This innovative manufacturing method has earned Rekiseisha international acclaim, with its foil products used not only by the Imperial Hotel, the Imperial Household Agency, and Nishi Honganji Temple, but also by global luxury brands such as CHANEL and GUCCI.

U/M/A/A Inc. is a next-generation record label dedicated to bridging music and art—including media art, fashion, anime, games, manga, and technology—across Japan and the rest of the world. The label curates and delivers high-quality music that spans a wide range of genres, from club and electronic music to internet-driven styles such as Vocaloid and anime songs.

Founded by Masakazu “Hiro” Hiroishi—formerly of the legendary Alfa Records, the company that brought Yellow Magic Orchestra (YMO) to global prominence in the late 1970s—U/M/A/A Inc. was established with the mission of carrying forward YMO’s pioneering spirit and the innovation of techno-pop into the modern age.

We believe we’ve put together a really strong album this time.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
And to promote this new release, you will be touring Japan from April to June. What can your fans expect from these shows?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
This tour mainly features songs from the album, but we’re mixing in popular live tracks and making big changes to the setlist in each location! Whether you come to one show or two or three, we’ll make sure the live experience never gets boring!
    


https://youtu.be/SxzSYnV8d1w


    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
What can you tell us about the evolution of nano.RIPE, both musically and as a duo, over the past two decades since you first started?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Although we’ve gone through several member changes, I’m really glad we’ve been able to keep going without stopping. When the members change, the sound naturally changes too, but that’s why we’ve made a point of clearly deciding which parts should change and which should stay the same. By focusing on creating music that stays true to nano.RIPE, I feel we’ve been able to grow.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Speaking of growth, how would you describe the new sound of Hikari wo Hakobumono and its theme of "initial impulses"?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
This is the 15th year since our debut, and our eighth album, but we still have plenty we want to do and sing about. I think that’s because the “initial impulse” we had when we started the band is still with us. This album is packed with that feeling.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
At Honey's Anime, we're thrilled about your new album, and many of your fresh tracks have been stuck in our heads since the first listen. Could you share a message with our readers who have been following your successful career?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Thank you so much for always supporting nano.RIPE! We’ll keep working hard to create great music. We look forward to the day we can meet at a live show.			
    





    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
      
We certainly be attending one—or more—of your shows this year!

title: [Honey's Anime Interview] Rico Sasaki on Palette Days and Her Creative Journey
text:
With a growing list of anime credits and a voice that effortlessly bridges the worlds of music and performance, Rico Sasaki continues to leave her mark across Japan’s entertainment scene. In this exclusive interview, she shares her excitement over performing “Palette Days”, the opening theme for Welcome to Japan, Ms. Elf!, and dives into her unique process behind voicing the charming cat-boy Mewi. 
	
	From heartfelt songwriting to her dreams of voicing unexpected roles, Rico Sasaki opens up about her passion, versatility, and the joy she finds in connecting with fans through both music and character.



		
 
	
    	
			Rico Sasaki




 

    
         Honey-Chan





Interview with Rico Sasaki
[gray-hex-decoration]

    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Ms. Sasaki, thank you so much for taking the time to chat with us. It’s a real pleasure to learn more about one of our favorite artists!				
					
You've had several years of career and nearly a dozen appearances in anime. How are you feeling about your song "Palette Days" being chosen as the opening theme for the anime Welcome to Japan, Ms. Elf!?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
When I heard I was chosen for the theme song, I was truly thrilled and honored! I was also happy when I passed the audition for the role of Mewi, and to be entrusted with the opening theme song as well! I almost jumped for joy.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
And this isn't your only anime involvement this year. You recently performed as Doloris in the opening of BanG Dream! Ave Mujica and will also be voicing a character in the upcoming Isekai Mokushiroku Mynoghra. How do you personally relate to Welcome to Japan, Ms. Elf!? and what is the connection between your song "Palette Days" and this anime?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Every show has a completely different world, and getting to both act and sing in each one is truly fun and fulfilling! In Welcome to Japan, Ms. Elf!, I play Mewi, a cute cat-boy with the special ability to control magic stones. To fully bring out his charm, I read the original manga thoroughly, watched cat videos to study their meows, and practiced really hard!
    


https://youtu.be/CO3RPKGAUr8


    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
While "Palette Days" was composed and arranged by KOUGA, with lyrics by Erica Masaki, another track on your latest single was written and composed by you. Could you tell us more about this particular song?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
“Kimi to Boku no Hoshi” is a song about cherishing and never forgetting emotions—even loneliness and sadness—and turning those feelings into the strength to face tomorrow, with a firm resolve to become a star. It’s like a wish carried on a shooting star. To stir the listener’s imagination, I intentionally used vague expressions, kept the instrumentation simple, and went through many rounds of trial and error, repeatedly sharing my vision as we shaped the song.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
You've had a notable career as a voice actress. How do you balance your time between your roles as a singer and an actress? What excites you the most about each?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Through singing, I can express my true, unfiltered emotions as Rico Sasaki. Through voice acting, I can become someone entirely different. Both are irreplaceable sources of purpose in my life, and getting to pursue something I’ve loved since I was young brings me more joy than anything else.
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
As an artist with such a distinctive voice, how do you prepare vocally for such varied projects like singing and voice acting? Do you have any special routines?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Eating well and getting plenty of sleep! No matter how motivated or excited I am, if I’m not healthy, I can’t give 100%, and I’d definitely regret that. So before a performance, I’m extra careful about taking care of myself. I also read lots of messages from fans. Even when I’m feeling anxious, their words calm me and make me want to see everyone right away. It instantly blows my fatigue away!		
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
And to wrap up the interview, is there any unexpected type of role you'd like to voice in the future, such as a ruthless villainess, a quirky mascot character, or something along those lines?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
I’d love to try voicing a handsome young man! I’ve played young boys around elementary school age before, but I’ve never had the chance to voice a teenage or adult male character, so I’d really like to try it. I’ll study hard to deliver a cool performance that gets everyone’s hearts racing!	
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
      
Thank you again, Ms. Sasaki, for sharing your time and insights with us. We’re excited to see what the future holds for you—both on stage and on screen—and we’ll be cheering you on every step of the way!

The Season 2 ending theme, “Ran,” performed by ASUKA, features a powerful yet delicate vocal performance that captures the show’s emotional depth and highlights its characters’ inner struggles.

	Message From Angelina 1/3 (Gacharic Spin)
“I had the honor of singing as one of the voices in the world of LINK TRAVELERS, standing alongside characters who fight through despair in search of light and strength.
It means so much to me to be part of this powerful project, especially with the incredible Eijun-san, whose work I deeply admire.
The songs Eijun-san writes always give me the strength to move forward and take me to new places.
I hope this song can be a source of strength for everyone out there fighting for their own freedom, just like the characters in LINK TRAVELERS.”

	Message From Eijun (THE BACK HORN)
“When creating this song, I focused on capturing the thrilling sense of adventure and the cool, stylish universe of LINK TRAVELERS.
I wanted the track to feel powerful and liberating, almost like breaking free from the everyday and reaching out toward freedom.
Angie’s rock vocals are truly one of a kind, and they brought the song to life with incredible energy.

title: [Honey's Anime Interview] STEREO DIVE FOUNDATION’s RON Reflects on 10 Years of Hits and Musical Evolution
text:
[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url=" ]
  



Celebrating a decade of genre-blending innovation and emotional resonance, STEREO DIVE FOUNDATION—helmed by the multi-talented artist and producer RON—marks its 10th anniversary with the release of "STEREO DIVE 03." In this interview, RON reflects on his evolution as a creator, the balance between artistic vision and collaboration, and the deeply personal threads woven through his latest work.




    
 

    
      RON 




 

    
         Honey-Chan






Interview with RON from STEREO DIVE FOUNDATION
[gray-hex-decoration]



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
RON, thank you very much for this opportunity! It's great to have you back, and congratulations on the 10th anniversary of STEREO DIVE FOUNDATION! Looking back on the past decade, how has your sound evolved since the release of your debut track “Daisy”? 
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
Over the past decade, I’ve written many songs, not only for myself but also as a music producer for others. Through my various experiences as a musician, I feel that the process of translating musical ideas in my head into concrete output has become more refined. I also sense that my creative repertoire has significantly expanded.
    




    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Your new album 'STEREO DIVE 03' features a mix of tie-up songs with anime, as well as original tracks. How do you balance the demands of working on anime theme songs with your personal musical vision?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
I primarily approach my work in a way that aligns with the anime. From my creative repertoire, I carefully select the musical elements that best suit the series. For parts beyond the first verse that aren’t used in the anime, I sometimes take a more personal approach.
    




    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
You’ve mentioned that the song '#03', which opens the album, represents your feelings of “looking forward to the future.” Can you explain more about the meaning behind the track and how it ties into your current journey as an artist?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    

To mark the 10th anniversary, I wanted to include a special touch. By bringing the intro phrase of “Daisy” to the very end, I aimed to express respect for the beginning while also conveying a sense of appreciation for what’s to come.
    


https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=haQ1-nHFE1I


    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Given that you’ve worked in many different contexts throughout these years, how have these experiences shaped your musical style and the way you connect with your audience? And how is that reflected in 'STEREO DIVE 03'? 
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
In recent years, I’ve had more opportunities to perform in front of overseas audiences. The song “HIKARI,” which is included in the album, was created specifically as a piece that could be sung together with them. When I performed it live, I truly felt a sense of unity, which was an awesome experience.
    




    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Your work as a composer spans multiple genres, from rock to EDM to orchestral arrangements. How do you decide which genre best fits the emotional tone of a song, especially when it’s tied to an anime series?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
I generally strive to write music in line with the request. When given full creative freedom, I refer to the script, storyboard, or any available footage to determine the appropriate genre and instruments for the scene.
    




    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
Do you have any favorite anisong from your own repertory? If so, which one and why?
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
It’s hard to choose just one, but if I had to, I’d say “STORYSEEKER.” I love both the melody and the arrangement. I put a lot of effort into it, even using custom sampling data that I created myself.
    




    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
With the 10th anniversary of STEREO DIVE FOUNDATION, what new goals and aspirations do you have for the future of your music and creative journey?        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
I want to reflect and think about what I truly want to create. I also aim to refine the balance between my own creative desires and external requests while deepening my mindset for pursuing what I love.
    




    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
        
We’re sure many Honey’s Anime readers have followed your journey, some from the very beginning. Is there anything you’d like to say to them as we wrap up the interview? 
        
    



    
        
            
            
                
                
            
        
    
    
I want to express my gratitude to those who discovered SDF or RON through anime. I’ll continue creating many more songs, so please look forward to them!
    






  
    Final Thoughts
  
  
  
With ten years of boundary-pushing music behind him, RON shows no signs of slowing down. As STEREO DIVE FOUNDATION enters its next phase, his commitment to authenticity, growth, and emotional connection remains unwavering. Whether through anime tie-ins or deeply personal tracks, RON continues to craft music that resonates across cultures and generations—inviting listeners to dive even deeper into the soundscapes he so passionately creates.		
		
As STEREO DIVE FOUNDATION looks ahead to a new chapter, we also look forward to many more songs from this amazing band. We've been here to appreciate these 10 years of music, and we'll continue to do so in the next decade too!

text:
[sourceLink asin="" asin_jp="" cdj_product_id="" text="" url="" ]
	



[en]What You Need to Know: [/en][es]Lo que necesitas saber: [/es] 


	MyAnimeList has unveiled the official list for the third annual “You Should Read This Manga 2025,” a global event designed to highlight exceptional new-and-upcoming manga available to the international fan. The final list, curated from 766 user nominated titles, features 77 unique manga series across four discovery categories.

	This highly-anticipated event aims to spotlight recently published manga and connect fans worldwide with new stories that deserve more recognition on a global scale. For 2025, the project continues to serve as a cultural bridge between creators, publishers, and readers in over 240 countries and territories.

	As an added incentive, MyAnimeList users who read 2 volumes of any title from the 2025 list during the campaign period will earn a time-limited profile badge.

	About “You Should Read This Manga 2025”?
A unique global manga promotion project carried out by world-renowned anime and manga community MyAnimeList in conjunction with industry professionals. The project is the first of its kind, using online nominations from users around the world to produce the ultimate list of manga recommendations for that year. Aside from the main category, “You Should Read This Manga,” the project includes a number of sub-categories, including series that fans would like to see animated.

	Categories & Criteria
	This global manga discovery project was launched with the goal of inspiring fans around the world to explore lesser-known but highly recommended titles. The final list is created from user-submitted nominations, which allows fans to vote for up to 10 titles and include persuasive reasoning for why each title should be featured. Titles must have seen an overseas release in 2024, and have a Score and Popularity ranking below #50 on MyAnimeList to be eligible for nomination. The 2025 edition includes four curated categories:
 
	You Should read This Manga 2025
For manga that readers simply really want to recommend to a friend!  
 (e.g. Gachiakuta, Magus of the Library, Kagurabachi)
 
	Should Be Anime
For manga not adapted into anime within the past 5 years. (e.g. Gokurakugai, Kindergarten Wars, Firefly Wedding)
 
	Best for Beginners
For new readers; short, accessible, or recently adapted into anime. (e.g. Dandadan, Smoking Behind the Supermarket with You, RuriDragon)
 
	Unique Art/Story
For seasoned manga fans seeking originality in artwork or narrative. (e.g. Veil, Kaiju Girl Caramelise, The Color of the End: Mission in the Apocalypse)

Explore the full list of selected works here: mxj.myanimelist.net/readthismanga/2025/nomination	
	
	Trends from This Year’s List	
	
	Demographic Balance: Half of the selected titles were originally published in shounen or seinen magazines. Notably, one in four of these titles received more votes from female readers.
	Digital Origins: 25% of the titles come from web-based manga platforms such as Shonen Jump+ or Manga UP.
	Anime Demand: Over half the “Should Be Anime” picks are shounen, with two-thirds of these available for free via MANGA Plus.
	Female Reader Influence: The “Unique Art/Story” list saw the majority of votes come from female users, in contrast to the other lists.
	Breakout Titles: Girls love/yuri manga The Guy She Was Interested in Wasn't a Guy at All had total nominations almost equal to all GL titles combined from the previous year. Likewise, new nominations for action manga Kagurabachi doubled any other action title.
	
	Additional Content
The project also features bonus recommendation sections created in collaboration with manga publishers and booksellers:
Try This Manga — for Free! → mxj.myanimelist.net/readthismanga/2025/try-manga
Publisher & Bookseller Picks → mxj.myanimelist.net/readthismanga/2025/more-recs
Kodansha Critical Hits & Fan-Favorites → mxj.myanimelist.net/readthismanga/2025/kodansha	
	
	About MyAnimeList
MyAnimeList is an anime and manga community, with comprehensive databases maintained by its passionate user base. The website allows members to track their viewing progress, rate and discuss titles, write reviews, and discover new works through various community-driven features. With over 19.5 million users from more than 240 different countries and territories, MyAnimeList is an essential resource for the international anime and manga fan.

The contest challenges writers to craft compelling stories based on one of two prompts:

	“The End is Now:” Dive into a world on the brink of destruction, where humanity has only one year left—how will people respond to the ultimate countdown?

Submissions will be hosted on Honeyfeed, a platform for aspiring novelists, from February 11, 2025, to May 7, 2025. 	Maaya Sakamoto’s latest song, “Drops,” has been chosen as the opening theme of the TV anime Aru Majo ga Shinu Made, which will premiere on April 1. A preview of the song is available in the first main promotional video for the series, released today.

	Aru Majo ga Shinu Made is a heartwarming fantasy about Meg, a 17-year-old apprentice witch, who is told by her long-lived teacher, Faust, that a terrible curse has left her with only one year to live. In order to break the curse, Meg sets out to bring happiness to those around her and collect the joyful tears shed by 1,000 people within a year.

	The lyrics for “Drops” were written by Yuho Iwasato, who has collaborated with Maaya Sakamoto on many songs. The music was composed by Naoto Kiyota, an up-and-coming composer making his debut collaboration with Sakamoto, and the arrangement was handled by Shin Kono, who has been arranging Sakamoto’s music for many years. This combination of familiarity and fresh talent makes for an exciting team.

https://youtu.be/l80FWPxqw_A
	
	About Maaya Sakamoto
Born in Tokyo, she began her career as a child actress at the age of eight. She made her CD debut in 1996 with the single “Yakusoku wa Iranai.” Following her 2011 album You Can’t Catch Me, which topped the Oricon chart, she began actively collaborating with a wide range of other artists and musicians. Since her 2013 album Singer-Songwriter, she has also been composing music for other artists.
In 2019, she released her 30th single “Uchuu no Kioku” (produced by Ringo Sheena) and her 10th original album Kyou Dake no Ongaku. In 2020, she released her 25th anniversary album Single Collection+ Achikochi and the digital single “Yakudo,” which topped the Oricon chart.

In July 2021, her radio program “Vitamin M,” which she had been hosting for 20 years, reached its 1,000th broadcast and entered its 21st year. In May 2022, she released the double tie-up single “Sumire / Kotoba ni Dekinai,” with music written and arranged by Shigeru Kishida.

To date, she has released 35 singles and 11 full albums. As a lyricist, in addition to writing her own original songs, she has also written many songs for other artists, including Kinki Kids’ “Hikari no Kehai,” Mamoru Miyano’s “Toumei,” and Walküre’s “Kaze wa Yokoku Naku Fuku,” and has published her own lyrics book Shishu (Kadokawa). 

She won the 38th Kazuo Kikuta Theater Award for her performance as Jerusha in the musical Daddy-Long-Legs. Her latest essay collection Manpukuron - Asu ni Kaburitsuke (Kadokawa) has also garnered attention.

In addition to her singing career, she is active as a voice actress, actress, lyricist, essayist, and radio personality. Her fresh and vibrant voice is loved by fans not only in Japan but also around the world. In 2025, she will celebrate her 30th anniversary as a performer and is set to contribute the opening theme song for the TV anime Aru Majo ga Shinu Made.

	Singer-songwriter Mekakushe teamed up with popular character Mamuang for her new song “Kimi wa Shunokeru” (You’re My Snorkel), which was released on January 15!

	The catchy, electro dance piece touches on the heart-wrenching feeling of not being able to breathe when a loved one isn’t around. This sentimental song was produced by Kaho Nakamura, Chelmico, Haruno, Harmoe, and Daoko, with Tomggg overseeing the whole collaboration.

The music video and CD jacket were also unveiled on the same day. These were designed by illustrator Wisut Ponnimit, who has worked with other top musical artists like Quruli, Haruoni Hosomo, Gen Hoshino, Ikuko Harada, and the poet Shuntaro Tanikawa.
	
	In the video, his star character, Mamuang, takes a deep dive to participate in an underwater singing competition, where she’s judged by a panel of marine life. The catchy tune is underscored by a sort of melancholy, which is beautifully portrayed in the animation. The whole piece showcases the best of Mekakushe and other hugely talented creators, so we hope that tons of people check it out!
	
	Mekakushe will also be performing with 2.5D artist Yuka Nagase, on Friday, February 7. Their joint concert, “Sekai ga Utsukushii Kara Dayo,” will be held at SHIBUYA PLEASURE PLEASURE, in Tokyo. 	Comment From Mekakushe
The hurt that comes with longing for someone is its own solemn sort of happiness.

From that fateful day onward, it feels like you’ve been set adrift at sea. The fragments of your shattered heart glisten on the water’s surface, and there’s the fear of slipping under the waves, to much darker depths. But, if you were with someone special, then even the bottom of the ocean could feel like heaven.

I’m not sure if that’s something to be happy or sad about, so it turned into a song.

Wisut Ponnimut, who designed the music video for “Kimi ha Shunokeru” is also the creator of “Happy Mamuang,” which has always been a protective charm for my heart. Those pictures and words have soothed me so many times. Just having my beloved Mamuang appear in the video is like a dream come true. When I saw the anime, I was so overcome with emotion, that I couldn’t get any words out. I won’t forget this, not even when I’m old and gray. Mamuang’s spirit lives inside my song.

	Comment From Wisut Ponnimut
Lively songs like this make you want to get up and move, so I did my best to match the animation to the rhythm, to make it feel like it was dancing. Hearing Mekakushe’s cute voice made me wonder what it would be like if Mamuang ended up in a much less adorable world.

Even when your surroundings are harsh, having someone to share them with—even for a moment—can make it all better. She has one line in the song that goes “stay just a little bit longer by my side,” and I could really feel that strong sense of gratitude at having met someone special. So, I worked that into the anime’s story, as well.

Life is so much bigger than anyone can imagine.
It’s a song that feels like taking a deep breath after breaking through the waves.

	Comment From Tomggg
When I first heard Mekakushe’s demo track, with her gorgeous song and simple piano, I couldn’t wait to figure out the best way to arrange the piece. It’s got a fascinating mix of warmth with a bit of a chill to it.

I hope that you’ll go with the ebb and flow of this song, letting it pull you along—whether you dive into it, or float along the surface.

	Artists Mekakushe and Yuka Nagase will hold a collaboration concert on February 7, 2025, at SHIBUYA PLEASURE PLEASURE!

	Additionally, on November 27, the song “Katsute, Chikyuu wa Shirokatta” (The Earth Was Once White)—the culmination of their collaborative project “Sekai ga Utsukushii Kara Dayo” (Because the World is Beautiful), an original three-part story told through music—was released for streaming. A delicate yet powerful Heisei-era-inspired pop song, it conveys a heartfelt wish to cherish the memory of a lost loved one.

	The music video and cover art accompanying the release were created in collaboration with illustrator Anbiyori, whose nostalgic style beautifully captures the essence of the Heisei era. Together, they deliver an immersive and intricately crafted experience. The song’s arrangement was performed by Kosuke Hayashi, frontman of the band Scenarioart, bringing yet another layer of artistry to this collaboration between rising talents.

The Mekakushe × Yuka Nagase Collaboration Live “Sekai ga Utsukushii Kara Dayo” will bring the story’s themes of the world’s end and imaginary friends to life through a full-band performance. Don’t miss this unforgettable event!

The Mekakushe × Yuka Nagase Collaboration Live is actually happening! I couldn’t be happier!

	About the song “Katsute, Chikyuu wa Shirokatta”
The astronaut Gagarin once said, “The Earth is blue.”

The blue of the Earth is the blue of the sea, reflecting only the blue light of the sun. Within that light lies the meteor shower of human tears, a blue of loneliness.

On the day the world ends, as we are flung into the vastness of space, what color will the Earth appear to be?
I want to sing while I can still remember. On this Earth, I want to keep singing together with Yuka-chan.

	Mekakushe Profile
Handling lyrics, composition, vocals, and piano performance by herself, the next-generation singer-songwriter Mekakushe enjoys immense popularity among artists and creators. Starting classical piano at the age of three, she gradually gravitated towards pop music. Her independently produced songs were featured in a Kao Laurier commercial, and she was one of the top artists on the Spotify official playlist “Kirakira Pop Japan” with a total of 3 million plays. She is a promising emerging artist with anticipated future success. 	Yuka Nagase’s Comment
I’m thrilled to announce that I’ll be performing in a two-artist concert with Mekakushe! This setup is a first for both of us, and I have a feeling it’s going to be something truly special. We’ll be delivering a world that only the two of us can create, so please come and experience it with us!

	About the song “Katsute, Chikyuu wa Shirokatta”
This track serves as the perfect conclusion to the “Sekai ga Utsukushii Kara Dayo” trilogy. Like the night sky, it reveals new landscapes with every listen.

When I first received the demo, I was struck by how much fresher and purer it sounded than I had imagined. Perhaps the end of the world really is like this.

I sang as though I were witnessing the end of the world from afar. Hidden within the song are countless delicate expressions and subtle breaths. Be sure to listen while gazing at the blue sky.

“Sekai ga Utsukushii Kara Dayo” Synopsis

I wanted you to tell me why I sing, why I’m drawn to loneliness.

Good morning, humanity.
On an ordinary morning, one thing was different:
the news of the world’s end burned itself into my sleepy eyes.

That night, I had the strangest experience.
In a dream, I met my imaginary friend.

As I wrote about the bizarre events in my dream diary,
I began to wonder who you were.
I no longer understood who I was.
I started to think about why I was alive.
I wanted to meet you.

Hey, if the world were to end in a week, what would you do?
	
	Yuka Nagase Profile
A datsuryoku-kei artist who works across 2D (Digital) and 3D (Physical) platforms.
She has a presence as both a virtual artist, using 3D CGI and illustrations, as well as a real-life artist, adapting her form of expression and performance depending on the medium.

In August 2023, she held her first solo live performance, “Eureka,” at Ebisu LIQUIDROOM. The tickets sold out in advance, and the live performance, which incorporated her 3D appearance, became a hot topic in the industry.

In September 2023, she released her first tie-up song, “Mujakina Kimochi.” The song was a special collaboration to celebrate the 20th anniversary of Tirol Choco’s popular “Kinako Mochi” product, and it gained over a million plays on TikTok. Also in September 2023, she released a mini album titled Launchvox. The album features contributions from emerging artists such as Pasocom Music Club, Mekakushe, Mao Sasagawa, Iyowa, and Amane Uyama and has earned recognition beyond the virtual artist scene.

X: x.com/yuka_n_RIOT
YouTube: hyoutube.com/@yukanagase	
	
	Kosuke Hayashi's Comment
I imagined this song as having such a grand scale that the two of them, cast into the atmosphere, could dye the Earth itself blue with their feelings. At the same time, I worked to craft a sound that stays close to the warmth of everyday life that’s always within reach.

For the chorus accompaniment, I combined the electric piano Wurlitzer with jazz piano, creating a sound that feels as if the two of them are playing back-to-back.

As I arranged the piece, I envisioned a beautiful, heartwarming end-of-the-world scene where they sing together with gentle smiles.
	
	Kosuke Hayashi'sProfile
While serving as the guitarist and vocalist for the twin-vocal band Scenarioart, he also engages in music production, arrangement, and artist producing. Notable works include projects with Sachiko Aoyama, formerly of Negoto, among others.

	Anbiyori’s Comment
I had the honor of working on the music video and cover illustration for this song. In preparing for this, I reread a dream diary I wrote several years ago, but most of the events seemed like a story written by someone else, as I had no memory of them.

Dreams feel as real as reality, and even when strange things happen, you accept them as part of that world, without a sense of discomfort. Yet, the moment you wake up, the details blur, and you realize it was all just a dream.

For this project, I created an illustration with the theme of a special place for just the two of them, where reality and dream memories blend together, much like when writing a dream diary. I hope you enjoy the beautiful song, which is gentle like a lullaby and embraces loneliness, along with the protagonist’s dream diary.
